_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

You were right on both counts — one was a **plotting bug**, one was **interpretation**.

### Why “median = 515” looked impossible

The left histogram had a hard-coded x-axis cap:

```python
player_bins = np.arange(0, min(160, ...), 5)  # ← capped at 160
```

So bars only covered **0–160 minutes**, but the median line was still drawn at **515** — in empty space. Worse, every player above 160 minutes was **dropped from the histogram** entirely, so the chart showed almost nothing past the floor spike while the stats box correctly reported median 515 on the full sample.

That’s fixed: bins now run out to ~p99 (~1,100 min), and the median line sits in the actual distribution.

### How median 515 makes sense (left panel)

This is **post–min-20** player-season minutes (54,582 rows, each ≥ 20 min):

- A **big pile** just above the floor (20–~100 min) — fringe rotation / low-minute guys who barely cleared the filter.
- A **long flat middle** (~300–900 min) — regular roster contributors.
- A **right tail** up to ~1,400+ — starters / high-minute players.

Median 515 means half of those **surviving** player-seasons are below 515 and half above. The floor spike pulls the median down; the long upper tail pulls it up. It is **not** “median of everyone near 20.”

### Layout fixes

- Stats box → **upper left**; legend → **upper right** (no more “without DFT” box on top of legend).
- Removed the **min-20 line on the right panel** (meaningless for team-mean minutes).
- Clearer subtitles: post-min20 on the left; same filtered panel on the right.

Regenerated: `REIGNING_BDP_minutes_player_team_mg10_min20_09_21.png`.

If you want the left panel even clearer, we could add a **log-y inset** for the floor spike or an **ECDF** alongside the histogram — say the word if you want that.

Both Alex plots are built on the **reigning lock** aperture (last-ps · mg10 · min20 · 09–21 · winsor 1–99 · ALLT · EW16 for the draft-rate plot).

### 1. Player poolq_LOO distribution
`basic_data_plots/REIGNING_BDP_poolq_loo_dist_mg10_min20_09_21_ppm_lastps.png`

- **Histogram + ECDF** of `poolq_loo` (leave-one-out teammate PPM z, excluding self)
- n = **22,795** last-ps rows; orange **+DFT** overlay (n = 9,483)
- Winsor clip spikes visible at ±0.6 (same artifact as existing LOO porch plots)

### 2. P(Y=1) vs player LOO
`basic_data_plots/REIGNING_BDP_draft_rate_poolq_loo_mg10_min20_09_21_ew16_ppm_lastps.png`

- **EW16 equal-width** bins on `poolq_loo` — same binning as reigning HERO
- Bar height = mean `Y_draft` per bin; vertical labels = bin n
- **LPM β₂ = +0.00172** — matches the lock readout in README
- Backing CSV + JSON alongside the PNG

### New code
- `sports/scripts/bdp_reigning_loo_plots.py`
- Wired into `reigning_hero_basic_plots.py` as `--only loo_dist` and `--only draft_rate_loo`
- **BDP slides deck** updated → **12 slides** (intro + 11 plots)

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

You're mixing two different x-axes that the codebase keeps separate. Here's the precise mapping.

## Reigning HERO lock = **player** `poolq_loo`, not team LOO

The slide-12 lock (`roster-x poolq_loo`, EW16, last-ps) bins **each player-season row** on that **player's** leave-one-out teammate mean:

$$\text{poolq\_loo}_i = \frac{1}{|T_j|-1}\sum_{k \in T_j,\, k \neq i} \hat{A}_k$$

- Computed **within** `(team_id, season)`, but **different for every player** on the roster (bench vs star see different teammate sets once you drop self).
- HERO then pools **all players** into 16 equal-width bins on that value and plots **mean `Y_draft`** per bin.
- So the porch plot we built is **correct for the reigning lock** — but the x-axis is **player LOO**, not a single team-level LOO average.

That's wired explicitly in `pass_a_empirical_bundle.py`: when `roster-x poolq_loo`, `roster_x` = each row's `poolq_loo`.

## The team-level alternative (what you may be remembering)

Pass A also supports `--roster-x poolq` (aliases: `team`, `pool_mean`, `T̂_j`). That sets:

```python
roster_x = groupby(team_id, season)["perf"].transform("mean")  # T̂_j, includes self
```

- **One x-value per team-season**, repeated on every player on that roster.
- Binning is still on **player-rows**, but the x-axis is **team mean Â** (includes self) — **not** LOO.
- **F-HERO** on your reigning population uses this team axis (`T̂_j`), not `poolq_loo`.

So the two roster-context choices in code are:

| Mode | X variable | Level | Includes self? |
|------|------------|-------|----------------|
| **`poolq_loo`** (reigning HERO) | Player LOO teammate mean | Per player-season | No |
| **`poolq` / team** (F-HERO) | `T̂_j` team-season mean perf z | Per team-season (tied across roster) | Yes |

There isn't a third canonical object called "team LOO average" in the pipeline — unless you **define** one (e.g. mean of player `poolq_loo` within a team-season), which isn't what HERO bins today.

## How the porch plots fit

| Plot | What it shows |
|------|----------------|
| **Â_i \| T̂_j** (`ai_tj`) | Distributions of player Â vs **team** mean (not draft rate) |
| **Â_i \| poolq_loo** (`ai_loo`) | Distributions of player Â vs **player** LOO |
| **T̂_j vs poolq_loo overlay** (`tj_loo`) | How wide team mean is vs tight player LOO |
| **HERO / draft_rate_loo** | **P(Y=1) vs player `poolq_loo` bins** — reigning lock |
| **F-HERO** | **P(Y=1) vs `T̂_j` bins** — team axis, paired sensitivity |

## Bottom line

You're **not wrong** that we've been binning roster context on the x-axis the whole time. For **reigning hero**, that context is **player-level LOO teammate quality**, not team-average LOO.

If Alex's ask was really **draft rate vs team mean** (`T̂_j`), that's the **F-HERO** family (or a new `--roster-x poolq` HERO run), not the reigning `poolq_loo` HERO.

If Alex meant "LOO computed within the team" — that's still **player** `poolq_loo`; teammates define it, but each player gets their own value.

Want me to add a porch plot **P(Y=1) vs `T̂_j`** (team axis, EW16) next to the player-LOO one so Alex can see both side by side?

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

You were right — the bottom-row hues were a leftover from the equal-width path, not something ventiles need.

**Why they were there:** `_paint_draft_rate_panel()` always called `_count_weighted_bar_colors()` — a Blues gradient keyed to bin **n**. That’s useful on the **top** row (equal-width bins), where counts pile up in the middle and thin out in the tails; darker bars flag sparse bins.

**Why they’re wrong on the bottom:** Quantile ventiles are built to have ~equal **n** per bin (~1,424 each). A count-based gradient is almost flat and reads like a second encoding of draft rate — misleading noise.

**Fix applied:** When `poolq_binning == "quantile"`, bars are flat `steelblue` (same as other BDP draft-rate panels). I also dropped the per-bin **n** labels on that row, since they’d just repeat the same number on every bar.

Top row unchanged: count-weighted hues + bin-n labels still there.

Regenerated `REIGNING_BDP_draft_rate_poolq_loo_vs_Tj_...png` and the slides deck.

## What Alex is asking (mechanically)

**Yes — mostly reruns, not new science.** The PD20–22 campaign already built the pipeline:

| Knob | Step | Existing script | Old default home |
|------|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **ρ** | ASSIGN — match sim sorting to empirical **H_sort** | `pd21_rho_hsort_calibrate.py` | `pd21_rho/` |
| **λ, γ, t** | SCORE + Bernoulli draft MLE on fixed rosters | `pd21_draft_bernoulli_mle.py` | `pd21_mle/` |
| **Temperature** | SELECT — Gibbs sweep (inverted-U survives?) | `grandchild_temperature_select_sweep.py` | `pd20_temperature/` |

What changes is **population spec**, not the math:

- **Seasons:** 2009–2021 (reigning lock), not 2011–21 / 13–21 campaign windows  
- **Filters:** min20 · mg10 · winsor · PPM z (same chain as HERO)  
- **Panel rows:** **last-ps** for HERO-facing fits; **all-ps** may still be right for ρ / roster-geometry (you already split this for BDP)

So: **wire reigning spec into those scripts → write to a new folder → compare numbers to old PD21 artifacts.** Some script flags may need extending (`--season-min 2009`, `last-ps` aperture for MLE) — that’s engineering, not reinventing calibration.

---

## Where to file new products (recommendation)

**Don’t scatter into `pd21_rho/` again.** That folder is tied to the **2011–21 campaign panel** and will confuse SI reviewers.

Extend what you already started:

```text
population_sandbox/reigning_hero/
  README.md                 ← population lock (exists)
  basic_data_plots/         ← porch BDP (done)
  hero/                     ← canonical HERO PNG + PASS_A tables (promote from sandbox/hero/)
  hero_star_sweeps/         ← bin×season sensitivity (done)
  fhero/                    ← paired F-HERO (done)
  calibration/              ← NEW — PD28 main line
    README.md               ← ladder step 3; script + aperture per subfolder
    manifest.json
    rho/                    ← ρ* vs H_sort
    mle/                    ← λ*, γ*, t*
    temperature/            ← Gibbs SELECT sweeps (sim; uses reigning roster sizes)
```

**Naming:** prefix everything `REIGNING_` or embed the slug in filenames, e.g.  
`REIGNING_PD21_rho_hsort_calibrate_09_21_mg10_min20_lastps.json`

Add `REIGNING_HERO_CALIBRATION` paths in `hero_gallery_paths.py` (same pattern as `REIGNING_HERO_BASIC_PLOTS`) so scripts have one canonical write target.

---

## Reorganization — why it feels lost

`HEROs_and_PASSes/` grew **two orthogonal axes** at once:

1. **Meeting/campaign axis** — `pd20_temperature/`, `pd21_rho/`, `pd22_minutes/` (PD20–22 HAND story)  
2. **Pass/ladder axis** — `pass_a/`, `pass_b/`, `pass_c_rho/`, `theta/`, `sort_chop_lambda/` (Wang ladder)

Plus a third layer you added correctly:

3. **Population axis** — `population_sandbox/reigning_hero/` (slide-12 lock)

No wonder the EDA march is hard to see. The fix isn’t one giant `mv` — it’s **declaring which axis wins for “paper-active” work**.

### Proposed mental model (paper march)

| Stage | Question | Active folder | Status |
|-------|----------|---------------|--------|
| **0** | Which population? | `reigning_hero/README.md` | ✓ Locked |
| **1** | Does the data look sane? (SI porch) | `reigning_hero/basic_data_plots/` | ✓ Done |
| **2** | What’s the hero shape? | `reigning_hero/hero/` + `fhero/` | ✓ Done |
| **3** | Calibrate ASSIGN/SCORE/SELECT | `reigning_hero/calibration/` | **← PD28** |
| **4** | Generative match / Pass B | `pass_b/` (outputs tagged reigning) | Next |
| **5** | Predictions (PD14, etc.) | TBD under reigning or `pass_a/` | Parked |

Everything not on that path is **campaign archive**, not deleted.

### Physical layout (phased — no big-bang)

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Great question — the overlap figure and **ρ\*** are answering different things.

## Why intervals “move with means” but ρ\* ≈ 0

**Interval overlap** shows **geometry on the talent axis**: each team-season is a window \([\min \hat{A}, \max \hat{A}]\) on PPM \(z\). Better teams have higher \(\hat{T}_j\), so their windows shift right — that’s visible stacking/shift. Your overlap meta also shows ~91% of the perf grid is covered by **more than one** team — heavy overlap, not disjoint tiers.

**\(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\)** is different. It’s the **realized sorting index**:

\[
H_{\mathrm{sort}} = 1 - \frac{\sum_i (A_i - \mu_{\text{team}(i)})^2}{\sum_i (A_i - \bar{A})^2}
\]

i.e. what fraction of total variance is “explained” by team assignment. On the reigning all-ps panel:

- **Pooled empirical \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) ≈ 0.064** (only ~6% of variance sorted into teams)
- **Per season:** roughly **0.057–0.073** (fairly tight band)

So rosters **look** structured on the axis (windows track team quality), but **within-team dispersion still dominates** — weak homophily in the \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) sense.

**ρ\* = 0** is the LG **assign** knob calibrated to match that index. From your reigning calibration, **ρ = 0 sim already gives \(H_{\mathrm{sort}} \approx 0.082\)** (mean over 650 draws) — **above** empirical ~0.064. The bracket stops at 0 (ρ can’t go negative), so ρ\* = 0 means: *even random LG assignment on real roster sizes overshoots empirical sorting slightly* — real NCAA assignment is **less** sorted than the sim at ρ = 0, not more.

Overlap = “where do team windows sit?” · \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) / ρ = “how much variance is team-assignment sorting?”

---

## New plot

**`REIGNING_BDP_Hsort_dist_mg10_min20_09_21_ppm_allps.png`**

- **Left:** per-season empirical \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) (bars) + LG ρ = 0 sim mean ± sd (orange)
- **Right:** histogram of all ρ = 0 sim draws vs pooled empirical line

Also: `*_by_season.csv` and `*.json` in `basic_data_plots/`.

Regenerate:
```bash
python sports/scripts/reigning_hero_basic_plots.py --only hsort_dist
```

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Yes — and it’s probably the **most direct** plot of the three, given what you already have.

**Decomposition (exact, per player):**

\[
A_i - \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i \;=\; (A_i - \hat{T}_j) \;+\; (\hat{T}_j - \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i)
\]

So the orange vs blue residual curves differ only by this **adjustment term** \(\hat{T}_j - \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i\). With player-level corr ≈ **0.9997**, the shapes track because that adjustment is **small and highly structured**, not because team and LOO are unrelated.

**What \(\hat{T}_j - \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i\) means:**
- Same \(\hat{T}_j\) for everyone on a team-season
- \(\mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i\) varies by player (excludes self)
- So this is **“how much including me shifts the local context”**
- Sign: above-average players → \(\hat{T}_j > \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i\) → positive; below-average → negative
- Magnitude grows with \(|A_i - \hat{T}_j|\) and shrinks with roster size (self matters less on big rosters)

**Why it’s worth plotting:**
1. Explains why LOO residuals are wider (σ **1.05** vs **0.97**) without re-plotting both curves
2. Makes the “self-inclusion” mechanism visible in one object
3. Natural follow-ups: vs roster size, vs \(A_i - \hat{T}_j\), +DFT purple overlay

**Caveat:** It’s **player-level** but **partly team-constant** (same \(\hat{T}_j\) for teammates), so you may want a note that it’s not i.i.d. — still fine for a porch KDE.

**Verdict:** Worth it — it’s the missing piece that turns “two nearly identical residual distributions” into a concrete story about self vs teammates.

### Your \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) + LOO question

The plot header compares both indices (same denominator \(\sum(A_i-\bar{A})^2\)):

| Index | Value |
|-------|-------|
| \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{team}}\) | **+0.064** |
| \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{LOO}}\) | **−0.108** |

**LOO is conceptually cleaner for local assortativity** — it asks “how does my ability compare to the teammates I actually face?” without self-pull on the context. But **dropping it straight into the \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) formula is problematic:**

1. **Team assignment is a proper partition** — within-team SS ≤ total SS, so \(H_{\mathrm{sort}} \in [0,1]\) has a variance-decomposition meaning.
2. **LOO is player-specific, not a partition** — \(\sum(A_i - \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i)^2\) can **exceed** total SS (here by ~11%), so \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{LOO}} < 0\). That's not “negative assortativity”; the index wasn't built for this numerator.

**Better paths if you want LOO-based sorting:**
- **Redefine the index** — e.g. correlation of \(A_i\) with \(\mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i\) within team-seasons, then average; or \(R^2\) of regressing \(A_i\) on \(\mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i\) within teams.
- **Use LOO in the generative/sim layer** (where you already care about local context) and keep \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) as the team-partition diagnostic for \(\rho\) calibration.
- **Hybrid:** report both, with \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{LOO}}\) explicitly labeled as non-partition (not bounded).

**Bottom line:** LOO is the right *local* context measure for assortativity intuition, but I'd treat **\(H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{LOO}}\)** as a diagnostic spur to define a new LOO-native index — not a drop-in replacement for team-based \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) in the \(\rho\) bracket.

Want me to compute a within-team \(\mathrm{corr}(A_i, \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i)\) pooled index next for a fair LOO-vs-team comparison?

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Your read on the **MBB identification problem** is right. When both the built-in homophily knob and the realized sorting index sit near zero, you are not really *estimating* assortativity on this domain — you are **confirming a boundary case**. That is scientifically useful, but a bad place to force a sensitive calibration.

## Does LOO magnify assortativity?

**Probably not — at least not in the way you need for \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) / \(\rho\).**

What we already see on the reigning panel:

| Object | Value | Implication |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{team}}\) | **0.064** | Weak but positive team sorting |
| \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{LOO}}\) (drop-in) | **−0.11** | Not “more signal” — wrong object for that formula |
| corr\((A_i-\hat{T}_j,\; A_i-\mathrm{LOO}_i)\) | **0.9997** | Team vs LOO residuals are almost the same shape |
| \(\hat{T}_j - \mathrm{LOO}_i\) | \(\sigma \approx 0.09\) | Self-inclusion gap is tiny vs ability scale |

LOO is **not peeling off a hidden layer of team assignment**. It is mostly re-centering within the same team buckets, with a small player-specific tweak. In an open market like MBB, that tweak is real for the **advancement** story (local context, inverted-U, draft) — but it does **not** make cross-team homophily much more visible.

So LOO is “digging deeper” into **local roster context**, not into **who ends up on which team**.

## Why weak assortativity wrecks model testing

Two different zeros get conflated:

1. **\(\rho \approx 0\)** — the generative homophily parameter (LG assignment doesn’t need much team sorting to match data).
2. **\(H_{\mathrm{sort}} \approx 0\)** — realized ability variance explained by team labels (teams don’t separate much on perf).

When both are ~0:

- \(\rho\) calibration has **no slope** — sim \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) at \(\rho=0\) already brackets empirical.
- Any objective of the form “match \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) by moving \(\rho\)” is **flat**.
- Algebraically, terms that treat homophily as a **multiplier** or **variance partition** become ill-conditioned: small noise dominates, ratios blow up, and “which layer owns the zero?” gets ambiguous (environment vs assignment vs score).

That is not a bug in your code. It is **weak identification in a weak-homophily domain**.

## What I’d do strategically

**1. Split “sorting” from “advancement” on MBB.**

- **Sorting / \(\rho\):** Treat MBB as **\(\rho \approx 0\) fixed or bounded** — a result, not a free parameter to nail.
- **Advancement / score–select:** Keep calibrating \(\gamma\), \(\lambda\), temperature, draft structure on LOO and team context — that is where MBB still has bite (you already have non-trivial numbers there).

**2. Use Army as the homophily anchor; MBB as the boundary.**

Strong story: *same mechanism stack, homophily dial near zero in a national talent market, still get advancement geometry.* That is actually Wang-style — different domains stress different predictions.

**3. If you want a LOO-native “assortativity” index, define a new one — don’t patch \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\).**

Candidates that stay in \([0,1]\) or have clear meaning:

- Within team-season: \(\mathrm{corr}(A_i, \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i)\), then pool/average.
- Within-team \(R^2\) of \(A_i\) on \(\mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i\).
- “Local co-sorting”: do high-\(A_i\) players face tougher local LOO than low-\(A_i\) players **within** teams?

Those measure **local alignment**, not **partition of teams**. They may be slightly larger than \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\), but they answer a **different estimand** — and you’d need sim analogs at \(\rho=0\) vs \(\rho>0\) to see if LG moves them at all.

**4. Don’t expect LOO to rescue \(\rho\) on MBB.**

If the generative story is “teams don’t sort much on ability,” no redefinition of within-team context will manufacture cross-team homophily. LOO can sharpen **\(L_C\)** / pool-quality channels; it won’t turn MBB into Army.

## Bottom line

Your instinct — *weak assortativity makes this domain a bad testbed for the homophily knob* — is correct. LOO is the right tool for **local competitive context** (hero layer), not for **magnifying team-level assortativity**. On this panel, it mostly confirms that team and LOO residuals are the same object up to a tiny self-inclusion shift.

**Practical recommendation:**  
- **MBB:** lock or bracket \(\rho \approx 0\); report \(H_{\mathrm{sort}}\) descriptively; calibrate and test on advancement/draft/temperature.  
- **Army (+ future domains):** use as the homophily-identification arm.  
- **Optional next dig:** a proper LOO-local sorting index with a sim counterpart — only if you want a second diagnostic, not as a replacement \(\rho\) target.

If useful, I can compute pooled within-team \(\mathrm{corr}(A_i, \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i)\) and the team-mean analog side by side, plus check whether LG at \(\rho=0\) vs small \(\rho>0\) moves that index at all. That would tell you whether *any* LOO-based sorting metric is calibratable before you commit to it in the paper.

True Shooting **is** in the stack — the keys are just easy to miss. There is no bare `ts` alias.

## Where TS lives

| User key | What it is | Panel column | Source |

| **`ts_pct_box`** | True shooting % from ESPN box totals | `ts_pct_box` | No SR merge |
| **`tspct`** or **`ts_pct`** | True shooting % from Sports-Reference | `ts_pct_sr` | SR merge required |

**Box formula** (`panel_rebuild.py`):

\[
\text{TS\%} = \frac{\text{PTS}}{2 \times (\text{FGA} + 0.44 \times \text{FTA})}
\]

Canonical definitions: `sports/sports_pipeline/perf_metric.py` (lines 21–24, 77–81, 96–100).

That’s the right **kill criterion** — and it’s stricter than the H_sort ladder.

## What the ladder actually tells you

Higher **H_sort** on BPM / TS% / eFG% only says: *players on the same team look more alike on that axis.* That helps **ASSIGN (ρ)** identification. It does **not** automatically buy you a better **advancement** story.

For **Âᵢ vs LOO** (or draft rate vs LOO), a high-sorting metric can even make things **more** monotone: if team sorting is strong, ability and teammate context move together → boring positive slope, less room for crowding / inverted-U.

So SCOUT’s ladder is **necessary context for ρ**; it is **not sufficient** to justify switching the hero metric.

## Your gate (the one that matters)

> Alternate `perf` is only valuable if it **does not** give the naive **monotone increasing** readout on **outcome vs LOO** (or a clearly flat LPM with no concavity).

On **PPM · reigning last-ps**, you’re already there empirically:

- HERO LPM **β₂ ≈ +0.0017** → flat / not concave  
- Shape tags: “robust tail drop,” not a clean inverted-U  
- Meanwhile **sim** can still show inverted-U at reigning **λ, t** (temperature sweep) — so the **model** has curvature; **empirical PPM** doesn’t show it cleanly in the HERO bin plot

That’s exactly the “monotone / flat empirical vs structured generative” tension.

## What to ask SCOUT to produce (per metric)

Same porch as reigning hero, one row per `perf`:

| Check | Pass if… |
|--------|----------|
| **P(Y=1) vs poolq_LOO** (EW16, last-ps) | **Not** strictly monotone ↑; visible peak or tail drop |
| **LPM β₂** on poolq_LOO | Negative / clearly concave (not ≈ 0) |
| **Âᵢ vs LOO** marginal | Optional — expect positive corr on most metrics; **don’t** use this alone |

**Do not** promote a metric on H_sort alone.

## Honest prior

| Metric type | H_sort | Likely Â vs LOO / draft vs LOO |
|-------------|--------|--------------------------------|
| **PPM, minutes** | Low | Monotone / flat (opportunity + congestion) |
| **TS%, FG%, eFG%** | ~2× PPM | Maybe slightly less monotone; still skeptical |
| **BPM, PER, WS** | High | **More** team-aligned → often **more** monotone, not less |

So BPM helping ρ while **worsening** the HERO geometry is a real possibility. The metric fork might split: **BPM for ASSIGN**, **PPM for advancement** — only if the paper can defend two ability axes. That’s a heavy lift unless one metric clearly wins the LOO-shape test.

## Bottom line for this thread

- **ρ ≈ 0 on PPM** — keep locked for reigning MBB.  
- **γ, λ, t + Pass B** — proceed; that’s where fitting still has bite.  
- **SCOUT metrics** — valuable **only** if they break monotone draft-vs-LOO; otherwise they’re ρ side-quest only.

If you want a single SCOUT deliverable line: *“For each metric in the ladder, rerun reigning `draft_rate_loo` + LPM β₂; flag monotone vs non-monotone; ignore H_sort for promotion decisions.”* I can wire that as a disposable batch script when you’re ready — not mixed with the SCOUT glossary work.

## Questions to nail down (worth one Alex sentence each)

### 1. Which **temperature**?

You have two:

- **t*** in MLE — softmax temperature in **score** (Bernoulli draft MLE).
- **Gibbs t** — temperature in **SELECT** (grandchild sweep).

For “generate draftees,” clarify: **Bernoulli draws from season softmax** (MLE world) vs **Gibbs top-K** (SELECT world). They can disagree; pick one primary for the HERO replay.

### 2. What is **L^C** in the fit vs in the sim?

PD21 MLE uses **`pool_c_smooth_team`** on empirical rosters, not raw `poolq_loo`. HERO porch plots use **poolq_LOO** on **PPM z**.

**Inconsistency risk:** fit on one local-context definition, HERO readout on another. Align before comparing plots (either refit with LOO-based L^C or build sim HERO on the same L^C the MLE used).

### 3. How are **draftees** generated?

- **Bernoulli** per player-season (MLE likelihood) — variable draft class size.
- **Fixed K** per season (empirical draft count) — **SELECT** proper.

HERO is usually **who got drafted**; K-matched SELECT is closer to “generate draftees” in plain language.

### 4. **HERO aperture** must match

Empirical reigning lock: **last-ps · ever-Y · EW16 · LOO · PPM z · min20 · mg10 · winsor**.

Sim HERO must use the **same** binning, row set, and LOO definition on **sim-selected** draftees (or full roster with Y_sim=1).

### 5. **γ** in this path

γ sharpens **viability / L^C** in the full LG story. Confirm the **empirical-roster draft generator** uses the **same γ*** as `pd21_draft_bernoulli_mle.py`, not a stale `tier1_sim_config` default.

### 6. What this **cannot** test

With frozen rosters you **cannot** claim:

- homophily / ρ calibration,
- “league formation” predictions,
- ASSIGN-layer Pass C ρ ablations.

You **can** claim:

- given real MBB rosters, do calibrated **score + select** reproduce **draft vs LOO** shape (monotone vs inverted-U, tail drop, etc.)?

That matches parking homophily.

### 7. **PPM vs SCOUT metrics**

Your gate still holds: alternate `perf` only matters if **draft vs LOO** isn’t naive monotone. Alex’s plan doesn’t require metric shopping unless SCOUT finds a non-monotone HERO — **keep PPM** for this replay unless that changes.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

You’re right to push back — the old “open question” was worded like you hadn’t chosen. **You did.** Here’s the blown-up version **with formulas**.

---

## Headline

**Bernoulli and softmax are not competitors.** They are **step 3 + step 4 of fitting.**

**Gibbs is not a replacement for Bernoulli.** It lives at **SELECT** — a later step, after scores exist.

Binding rule (score ≠ select): [`BINDING_Selection_is_its_own_step.md`](3-Master_Plan/BINDING_Selection_is_its_own_step.md)

---

## The pipeline (with math)

On **frozen empirical rosters**:

```
ASSIGN (given)  →  SCORE  →  SOFTMAX  →  BERNOULLI ℓ  →  [fit done]
                                                      ↓
                                              SELECT (generate Y^sim)  →  HERO plot
```

---

### 1. SCORE — what goes into the board

**Conceptual Alex score** (binding doc):

\[
S_i = A_i - \lambda\, L^C_i
\]

- \(A_i\) = ability (PPM z, reigning lock)
- \(L^C_i\) = local crowding (MLE uses `pool_c_smooth_team`; HERO x-axis uses `poolq_loo` — separate open question)
- \(\lambda\) = how much congestion enters the **ranking**

\(\gamma\) does **not** sit in this line. It sharpens how \(L^C\) is **built** from teammate viability. You fit \(\gamma^* \approx 19.57\) jointly with \(\lambda^*\) and \(t^*\).

---

### 2. SOFTMAX — turn scores into season weights

**PD21 board logits** (what `pd21_draft_bernoulli_mle.py` actually uses):

\[
\eta_i = \frac{A_i}{t_{\mathrm{MLE}}} - \lambda\, L^C_i
\]

**Watch this:** it is **not** \((A_i - \lambda L^C_i)/t_{\mathrm{MLE}}\). Talent is divided by \(t\) **before** subtracting congestion. That’s the “PD21 board form.”

Within each draft season \(s\), softmax gives relative weights that sum to 1:

\[
p_i = \frac{\exp(\eta_i)}{\sum_{k \in s} \exp(\eta_k)}
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
\sum_{i \in s} p_i = 1
\]

So \(p_i\) = “share of draft probability mass” in that season — a **closed pool**, not yet independent coin flips.

---

### 3. BERNOULLI — how we **fit** (already decided)

Treat each real draft outcome \(Y_i \in \{0,1\}\) as an independent Bernoulli trial with probability \(p_i\):

\[
\ell(\lambda, \gamma, t_{\mathrm{MLE}})
= \sum_i \Big[ Y_i \log p_i + (1-Y_i)\log(1-p_i) \Big]
\]

Maximize \(\ell\) → reigning numbers:

\[
\gamma^* \approx 19.57,\quad \lambda^* \approx 1.30,\quad t^*_{\mathrm{MLE}} \approx 1.07
\]

**That’s the decision:** fit with **softmax → Bernoulli log-likelihood**. Script name says it: `pd21_draft_bernoulli_mle.py`.

We **also** check top-\(K\) overlap (do highest \(p_i\) match draftees?) — diagnostic only, **not** the likelihood.

---

### 4. Two temperatures — same letter, different jobs

| | **\(t_{\mathrm{MLE}}\)** | **\(t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}\)** |
|---|--------------------------|----------------------------|
| **Where** | Inside \(\eta_i = A_i/t - \lambda L^C\) **before** softmax | Inside \(\exp(S_i/t)\) at **SELECT** |
| **Fitted?** | Yes — \(t^* \approx 1.07\) | No — swept \(\log_{10} t \in [-3,3]\) |
| **Plain English** | How sharply talent separates the \(p_i\) table | How much **luck** is in who gets the \(K\) slots |

**MLE \(t\):** small \(t\) → one superstar hogs probability mass; large \(t\) → \(p_i\) flatten.

**Gibbs \(t\):** small \(t\) → almost always take top \(K\) by score; large \(t\) → noisy lottery among plausible players.

You ran **both** in reigning calibration: MLE for \((\gamma,\lambda,t_{\mathrm{MLE}})\); temperature sweep for Gibbs SELECT at \(\rho=0\).

---

### 5. SELECT — Gibbs (also already in codebase)

When Alex says “generate draftees,” he means **pick winners** after parameters are fixed.

**Grandchild / PD20 score** (SELECT sweeps):

\[
S_i = A_i - \lambda^* L^C_i
\]

**Gibbs rule D** — weights and \(K_s\) draws without replacement:

\[
w_i \propto \exp\!\left(\frac{S_i}{t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}}\right),
\qquad
\text{draw } K_s \text{ players proportional to } w_i
\]

(\(K_s\) = actual draft class size that season.)

**Three generative options** (this is what’s still open for HERO replay v1):

| Rule | Formula / mechanism | Class size |
|------|---------------------|------------|
| **Top-\(K\)** | \(Y^{\mathrm{sim}}_i=1\) iff \(i\) in top \(K_s\) by \(p_i\) or \(\eta_i\) | Exactly \(K_s\) |
| **Bernoulli replay** | \(Y^{\mathrm{sim}}_i \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_i)\) i.i.d. | **Random** |
| **Gibbs** | \(K_s\) draws from \(\exp(S_i/t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}})\) | Exactly \(K_s\), noisy |

---

### 6. HERO — outcome plot (not in the fit)

HERO doesn’t use softmax or Gibbs directly. It bins by LOO pool quality and plots draft rate:

\[
\hat{r}_b = \frac{\sum_{i \in \text{bin } b} Y_i}{|b|}
\]

Compare empirical \(Y_i\) vs sim \(Y^{\mathrm{sim}}_i\) on the **same** EW16 LOO bins.

---

## Baby numeric example (one mini-season, 3 players)

Suppose in one draft year:

| Player | \(A_i\) | \(L^C_i\) | \(\lambda=1.3\), \(t_{\mathrm{MLE}}=1.07\) |
|--------|---------|-----------|---------------------------------------------|
| Star | 2.0 | 0.5 | \(\eta = 2.0/1.07 - 1.3(0.5) \approx 1.22\) |
| Mid | 0.5 | 0.0 | \(\eta \approx 0.47\) |
| Role | -0.5 | 1.0 | \(\eta \approx -1.77\) |

Softmax → something like \(p \approx (0.62,\, 0.33,\, 0.05)\) (sums to 1).

- **Bernoulli fit** asks: does \(Y_{\text{Star}}=1, Y_{\text{Mid}}=0, Y_{\text{Role}}=0\) make sense under those \(p_i\)?
- **Top-\(K\)** with \(K=1\) → draft Star only (deterministic).
- **Gibbs** with \(K=1\), small \(t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}\) → almost always Star; large \(t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}\) → Mid sometimes wins.

---

## What you already decided vs what’s still open

**Decided:**
- Fit: **softmax + Bernoulli** (PD21 Alex lock) ✓
- Reigning \((\gamma^*, \lambda^*, t^*_{\mathrm{MLE}})\) ✓
- SELECT sensitivity: **Gibbs sweep** (PD20) ✓

**Still open (narrow):** For empirical-roster HERO replay, which SELECT rule wires \(Y^{\mathrm{sim}}\) by default — top-\(K\), Bernoulli replay, or Gibbs + which \(t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}\) from the sweep? That’s a one-line Alex call, not “did we pick Bernoulli or Gibbs ever.”

---

I added a **Formula sheet** section to [`MBB_empirical_roster_select_replay.md`](3-Master_Plan/re_entry/HEROs_and_PASSes/MBB_empirical_roster_select_replay.md) so you can re-PDF when ready. The subtle PD21 vs grandchild point worth memorizing:

\[
\underbrace{\eta_i = \frac{A_i}{t_{\mathrm{MLE}}} - \lambda L^C_i}_{\text{PD21 fit (softmax input)}}
\quad\neq\quad
\underbrace{\frac{A_i - \lambda L^C_i}{t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}}}_{\text{not what either script uses}}
\]

PD21 scales **\(A\)** by MLE \(t\); Gibbs scales **\(S=A-\lambda L^C\)** by a **different** \(t\) at SELECT only.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**Logits** = the **raw scores** you feed into softmax **before** they become probabilities. They can be any real numbers (positive, negative, big, small). Softmax squashes them into \(p_i\) that sum to 1.

**Board logits** = Alex’s name for those raw scores on the **draft board** — the within-season ranking table for “who gets how much draft mass this year.” “Board” is whiteboard language from PD21, not a special math object.

---

## The one formula

For player \(i\) in draft season \(s\):

\[
\eta_i \;=\; \frac{A_i}{t_{\mathrm{MLE}}} \;-\; \lambda\, L^C_i
\]

In code this is `board_logits`:

```172:175:sports/scripts/pd21_draft_bernoulli_mle.py
def board_logits(ability: np.ndarray, lc: np.ndarray, *, lam: float, t: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """PD21 board: A/t − λ L^C (not (A − λ L^C)/t from sim SCORE)."""
    t_safe = max(float(t), 1e-12)
    return ability / t_safe - float(lam) * lc
```

- \(\eta_i\) = board logit for player \(i\) (we sometimes write \(\mathrm{logits}_i\))
- \(A_i\) = ability
- \(L^C_i\) = local crowding
- \(\lambda\) = congestion weight
- \(t_{\mathrm{MLE}}\) = MLE temperature on ability

**Higher \(\eta_i\)** → player looks better on the board → **higher** draft probability after softmax.

---

## Why “logits” and not just “score”?

Alex score is \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L^C_i\). Board logits are a **reparameterization** for the **draft-probability** step:

\[
p_i \propto \exp(\eta_i)
= \exp(A_i/t)\cdot \exp(-\lambda L^C_i)
\]

So the board **factorizes** into:
- talent term: \(\exp(A_i/t)\)
- congestion penalty: \(\exp(-\lambda L^C_i)\)

“Logits” means: **the thing inside the exponential** (up to an additive constant per season). If \(\eta_i\) goes up by 1, odds ratio \(p_i/(1-p_i)\) doesn’t simply multiply — but **relative** weight vs another player multiplies by \(e^1\).

Then softmax makes them proper probabilities:

\[
p_i = \frac{\exp(\eta_i)}{\sum_{k \in s} \exp(\eta_k)}
\]

Only **differences** between \(\eta_i\) matter for ranking within a season; adding the same constant to everyone doesn’t change \(p_i\).

---

## Baby example (3 players, one season)

| Player | \(A_i\) | \(L^C_i\) | \(\eta_i = A_i/1.07 - 1.3\,L^C_i\) |
|--------|---------|-----------|-------------------------------------|
| Star | 2.0 | 0.5 | \(\approx 1.22\) |
| Mid | 0.5 | 0.0 | \(\approx 0.47\) |
| Role | −0.5 | 1.0 | \(\approx −1.77\) |

Softmax → roughly \(p \approx (0.62,\, 0.33,\, 0.05)\).

- **Logits** = \((1.22,\, 0.47,\, -1.77)\) — pre-probability scores  
- **\(p_i\)** = shares that sum to 100% — post-softmax  

Bernoulli fitting then asks: do actual draft outcomes \(Y_i\) match these \(p_i\)?

---

## What logits are **not**

- **Not** probabilities (they don’t sum to 1; Role’s is negative).
- **Not** the same as Gibbs SELECT weights (those use \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L^C\) and a **different** \(t\) at the SELECT step).
- **Not** \((A_i - \lambda L^C_i)/t\) — PD21 puts \(1/t\) on **\(A\) only**, not on the whole score.

---

**One-liner:** *Board logits = the draft-board raw scores \(\eta_i = A_i/t - \lambda L^C_i\) that softmax turns into season draft probabilities \(p_i\).*

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Good — **Gibbs K-draw (rule D)** is now the v1 lock for the empirical-roster replay. I updated the memo with that decision plus a **SELECT history** section.

---

## How we SELECTed before

**For generative sim (assign → score → select → HERO): yes, almost always top-K.**

The codebase has four winner rules in `tier1_pool_assignment.py`:

| Rule | What it does | Our usage |
|------|--------------|-----------|
| **C** | Deterministic **top-K** by score \(S_i\) | **Default everywhere** — `tier1_sim_config.py`, 540 notebook, Pass A/B, PD17 λ sweep, most grandchild diagnostics |
| **D** | **Gibbs K-draw:** \(w_i \propto \exp(S_i/t)\), then \(K\) picks without replacement | PD20 temperature sweep, reigning calibration, **your new replay default** |
| **A** | Stochastic proportional sample (not Gibbs) | Older 537 experiments; not the main path |
| **B** | Bernoulli-ish independent coins | Older 537 experiments; not the main path |

**Timeline in plain English:**

1. **Tier1 / 540 / Pass A–B:** “Score everyone, take the top \(K\)” — rule **C**. That’s the BINDING v1 winner rule.
2. **PD17:** Same — top-K while sweeping \(\lambda\).
3. **PD20:** Introduced rule **D** (Gibbs) as a **gate**: does the inverted-U survive when select isn’t a hard cut? It did → green light for MLE.
4. **PD21:** **No SELECT step** — fitting uses softmax → Bernoulli on real draft outcomes. Top-K appears only as a **diagnostic** (“do highest \(p_i\) match actual draftees?”).
5. **Reigning calibration:** Gibbs sweep at \(\rho=0\) on 09–21.
6. **Next (replay):** Gibbs K-draw first; then you compare top-K and Bernoulli replay as sensitivities.

**Useful fact:** at very cold Gibbs \(t\), rule D **collapses to** rule C — PD20’s “cold limit” check showed they nest.

---

## Gibbs K-draw — what we’re wiring

Per season \(s\), with empirical draft count \(K_s\):

\[
S_i = A_i - \lambda^* L^C_i, \qquad
w_i \propto \exp\!\left(\frac{S_i}{t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}}\right),
\qquad
\text{draw } K_s \text{ players without replacement}
\]

Uses `choose_selected(..., choice="D")` from `tier1_pool_assignment.py` — same machinery as PD20.

**Parameters:** \(\gamma^*, \lambda^*, t^*_{\mathrm{MLE}}\) from PD21 fit; **separate** \(t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}\) for SELECT (start with \(t=1\) unless the sweep points elsewhere).

---

## What’s next

The replay script (`reigning_hero_sim_hero.py`) isn’t built yet — this is the decision lock. When you want to proceed, implementation order would be:

1. Gibbs replay → sim HERO vs empirical  
2. Sensitivity: top-K (rule C)  
3. Sensitivity: Bernoulli draws from MLE \(p_i\)

Say the word and I’ll start on step 1.

**Done.** Gibbs K-draw replay is implemented and all three SELECT methods have been run.

## What was built

**Script:** `sports/scripts/reigning_hero_sim_hero.py`  
**Outputs:** `population_sandbox/reigning_hero/sim_hero/`  
**Launcher:** `reigning_hero_sim_hero.zsh`

**Pipeline:**
1. Load all-ps panel (min20) — same pool as PD21 MLE  
2. Attach team $L^C$ at $\gamma^*$  
3. Per season: $S_i = A_i - \lambda^* L^C$, Gibbs rule D, $K_s$ = NBA draft count (`draft_year == season`)  
4. Career cap: each athlete drafted at most once  
5. HERO readout on last-ps · mg10 · EW16 LOO · ever-$Y$

## Results (09–21 reigning lock)

| SELECT | Sim drafted (last-ps) | LPM $\beta_2$ (sim) | vs emp $\beta_2 \approx +0.00172$ |
|--------|----------------------|---------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Gibbs** ($t=1$) | **617** | **+0.00004** | Essentially flat — matches empirical |
| **Top-K** | 616 | +0.03063 | More concave than emp |
| **Bernoulli** | 13 | −0.00167 | Variable $K$ — not a good generative match |

**Empirical drafted on last-ps:** 615

Main artifact:  
`sim_hero/REIGNING_SIM_HERO_gibbs_t1_mg10_min20_09_21_last_ps.png`  
(side-by-side empirical vs sim HERO bars)

## Re-run commands

```bash
# Gibbs only (default)
python sports/scripts/reigning_hero_sim_hero.py

# All three SELECT methods
python sports/scripts/reigning_hero_sim_hero.py --select all

# Different Gibbs temperature
python sports/scripts/reigning_hero_sim_hero.py --gibbs-t 0.1
```

## Bug fixes along the way

1. **$K$ per season** — must use NBA draft lookup (`draft_year == season`), not `sum(Y_draft)` on ever-labeled all-ps rows (that was double-counting multi-year players).  
2. **Career cap** — a player can only be sim-drafted once across seasons.

Bernoulli sensitivity is included for comparison; it is not meant to match fixed-$K$ draft class size. Next natural step: sweep Gibbs $t$ on this replay path (like PD20) or overlay all three SELECT curves on one figure.

Good sweep — it tells a coherent story once you remember **HERO bins LOO** but **SELECT ranks on** $S_i = A_i - \lambda^* L^C$ (team `pool_c_smooth_team`, not `poolq_loo`).

## What empirical looks like (left panel, every run)

- Gentle **upward** draft rate as LOO increases (~1.3% in the left tail → ~4% mid-right).
- LPM $\beta_2 \approx +0.0017$ → tagged “flat / not concave” (reigning lock).
- Shape tag still says `inverted_u_like` with peak around bin 13 — weak hump, not a dramatic inverted-U.

That’s your target.

---

## Gibbs $t$ sweep — the dial works as theory predicts

| $t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}}$ | Sim $\beta_2$ | What the sim panel looks like | Read |
|----------------------|-----------------|-------------------------------|------|
| **0.001** | **+0.031** | Tall bars on the **left** (low LOO) | Cold → ≈ top-K by $S$ |
| **0.1** | **+0.026** | Same — left-heavy | Still essentially cold |
| **1.0** | **≈ 0** | Relatively **flat** ~2–3% all bins | **Best match to empirical flatness** |
| **1.5** | +0.011 | Slight left lean | Warming up |
| **5** | −0.007 | Flatter, mild mid-hump | Moving toward lottery |
| **12** | −0.007 | Similar | Hot side |
| **50** | −0.003 | Nearly **uniform** ~2.5–3.5% | Hot → random $K$-draw |

**Top-K (rule C)** matches **cold Gibbs** ($\beta_2 \approx +0.031$) — same left-heavy sim shape. That’s the PD20 “cold nests top-K” result, now on **frozen empirical rosters**.

---

## The key insight (why cold looks “backwards” on LOO)

Cold SELECT picks the highest **$S = A - \lambda L^C$**, not the highest LOO.

Big-fish-small-pond players can have **high $A$ with low LOO** → they win top-$K$/cold-Gibbs slots → sim **over-drafts the left bins** on the LOO axis.

That’s not a bug in your code — it’s **score axis ≠ HERO axis**. Congestion in the score uses team $L^C$; HERO reads out on `poolq_loo`. Cold select is faithful to the score; the LOO porch punishes you for plotting on a different x-axis.

---

## What I’d take from this

**1. $t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}} \approx 1$ is the sweet spot for this replay.**  
It’s the only run that lands near empirical $\beta_2 \approx 0$ without the cold left-spike or hot noise. Your $t=1$ image is the one I’d show Alex first.

**2. The sweep validates the PD20 story on real rosters.**  
Cold → top-K pathology on LOO; hot → flat lottery; mid-$t$ → compromise.

**3. None of the runs fully clone the empirical *slope*.**  
Empirical drifts up with LOO; sim at $t=1$ is **flatter** (compressed 2–3% band vs emp 1.3–4%). You matched **curvature tag** (flat $\beta_2$) better than **bin-for-bin slope** — which is honest for v1.

**4. $t=50$ isn’t “wrong,” it’s the wrong comparison.**  
It’s nearly a uniform draft lottery — flat sim, no LOO gradient. Fine as a **hot-limit** anchor, not as a fit.

---

## Practical recommendation

- **Lock v1 replay at $t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}} = 1$** (maybe bracket 0.5–2 in a one-slide sensitivity strip).
- **Keep cold (0.001) and top-K** as “what happens if SELECT is too sharp” — illustrates LOO vs $L^C$ mismatch.
- **Optional next plot:** one figure, empirical line + sim curves for $t \in \{0.1, 1, 5, 50\}$ — would make the dial story one glance for Alex.

If you want, I can add a `--gibbs-t-sweep` mode to `reigning_hero_sim_hero.py` that produces that overlay PNG + a small $\beta_2$ vs $\log_{10} t$ table automatically.

- `...json` — full metadata

---

## Score axis vs HERO axis — what to do

This is **not** a bug to “fix” silently. Binding rule: **score ≠ hero**. You have two different objects:

| | **SCORE / SELECT** | **HERO (outcome plot)** |
|--|-------------------|-------------------------|
| **Question** | Who wins the draft slot? | What does draft rate look like vs LOO? |
| **v1 uses** | $S_i = A_i - \lambda^* L^C_{\mathrm{team}}$ (`pool_c_smooth_team`) | Bins on `poolq_loo` |

**Why cold Gibbs looks “backwards” on LOO:** SELECT ranks on $S$ (ability minus **team** crowding). HERO bins on **LOO** (leave-one-out teammate quality). Big-fish-small-pond players can score high on $S$ while sitting in **low-LOO** bins → cold/top-$K$ over-drafts the left side. That’s the mismatch showing up, and it’s actually informative.

### Recommended path (pragmatic)

**1. For Alex v1 — document + lock $t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}} \approx 1$**  
You already showed the dial works: $t=1$ matches empirical flat $\beta_2$ best. Caption the axis split explicitly. Use the new overlay PNG as the one-slide story.

**2. Next sensitivity (medium effort) — LOO-aligned SCORE, same $\lambda^*$**  
Rerun SELECT with `pool_c_smooth_loo` in $S$ instead of team $L^C$. Same HERO x-axis, no MLE refit yet. Answers: *“If congestion in the score used the same local object as the porch, does cold left-spike go away?”*

**3. Bigger lift — refit PD21 MLE with LOO $L^C$**  
So fit, SELECT, and HERO all speak the same congestion language. Only do this if Alex wants bin-for-bin alignment, not just flat $\beta_2$.

**4. Dual readout (you already have half)**  
Keep LOO HERO; pair with **F-HERO** on $\hat{T}_j$ (`fhero/`) so SELECT-vs-team-axis is visible too.

### What I would **not** do

- Silently change the HERO x-axis to team $L^C$ to force a match (hides the reigning lock).  
- Treat cold left-spike as “model failure” without naming the axis mismatch.  
- Jump to a new performance metric before trying LOO-in-SCORE sensitivity.

If you want step 2 wired next, I can add `--score-lc team|smooth_loo` to the sim script so you can A/B in one command.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Done — the overlay now has a **mid-$t$ inset** ($t \geq 0.75$, cold curves omitted) and the **$\beta_2$ panel** y-zooms to mid-$t$ with a note that cold points are off-scale.

### Are the sweep values good?

**Old grid** `(0.001, 0.1, 1, 1.5, 5, 12, 50)` was fine for a first pass, but:
- **0.001 ≈ 0.1** — both give $\beta_2 \approx +0.03$ (top-K pathology); one cold anchor is enough
- **Big gap 0.1 → 1** — misses the transition where curvature flips
- **50 ≈ 12** on the hot side — both flatten toward a lottery; one hot anchor suffices

**New default** `(0.1, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 5.0, 12.0)` is better for Alex:

| $t$ | $\beta_2$ | Role |
|-----|-----------|------|
| 0.1, 0.5 | +0.026, +0.023 | Cold / near–top-K (document, exclude from inset) |
| 0.75 | −0.009 | Transition into mid band |
| **1.0** | **+0.00189** | **Best match to emp (+0.00172)** |
| 1.5–2 | −0.007 to +0.009 | Local wiggle around flat |
| 5, 12 | −0.003, +0.006 | Hot / flatter lottery |

**Verdict:** Keep this grid for v1. **$t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}} = 1$** is still the clear lock — the new 0.75 point usefully brackets it. I would not add more points unless you want a fine scan in $[0.8, 1.2]$ (e.g. 0.85, 0.95, 1.1) to nail the $\beta_2$ crossing; eight curves is already readable.

**Note:** $t = 0.5$ is still “cold” in shape terms even though it’s in the main panel — that’s why the inset cutoff is **0.75**, not 0.5.

Reopen the PNG to see the inset; cold $t$ curves stay in the main panel for the top-K story but no longer squash the mid-$t$ zoom.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

That bottom panel is telling you something important — and it is **not** “temperature smoothly tunes curvature.”

### What you’re seeing

You swept **t linearly** (0.75 → 15), but the plot is **log₁₀ t** on the x-axis. Even so, β₂ wiggles: roughly **−0.019 to +0.014**, while empirical sits at **+0.0017**. So the whole sweep lives in a **±0.02 band around flat**, with no clean monotone trend.

The top panel matches that story: the curves are **interleaved spaghetti**, not ordered by t. If t were a clean shape dial, you’d expect cold curves left-heavy, hot curves flatter, with curves stacking in order. Instead they cross constantly.

### What I think it means

**1. β₂ is a brittle summary of a nearly flat object.**  
Empirical HERO is already flat (β₂ ≈ 0). You’re fitting a quadratic to a curve that has no real curvature. Small bin-level jitter in who gets drafted moves β₂ by amounts **larger than the empirical signal itself**.

**2. t reshuffles a discrete set of ~617 picks, not a smooth continuum.**  
Gibbs rule D + fixed K + career cap means changing t flips **which borderline players** get a slot. That’s a **composition change** (dozens of players in/out), not a smooth deformation of a HERO curve. β₂ can go up at t=5 and down at t=6 because different marginal guys crossed the line — not because “6 is colder than 5” in any HERO sense.

**3. SCORE axis ≠ HERO axis (the big one).**  
You’re dialing noise in **S = A − λLᶜ(team)** but reading curvature on **poolq_LOO**. Those are correlated but not aligned. Increasing t flattens selection in *score* space; the pushforward to LOO space has **no reason to be monotonic**. Oscillation is exactly what you’d expect when the knob and the readout live on different axes.

**4. Bin noise amplifies it in the top plot.**  
Those jagged ventile rates (~38 drafted per bin on average, unevenly) make the “inverted u like” tags flip constantly. β₂ is player-level LPM, but it’s still being driven by the same sparse draft counts.

### What I would **not** conclude

- Don’t read t=13’s dip (−0.019) or t=5’s peak (+0.014) as real “temperature phases.”
- Don’t claim a unique t* from β₂ alone beyond “somewhere near 1 the summary statistic crosses the empirical line” — t=10 is also near zero.

### What I **would** conclude (Alex line)

> **Mid–hot Gibbs t does not systematically tune LOO-HERO curvature.** Empirical HERO is flat; sim HERO stays in a flat noise band across t. **t ≈ 1 is a reasonable lock** (close to MLE board temperature, β₂ near empirical), but the β₂–t relationship is **weakly identified** here — mostly discrete reshuffling + axis mismatch, not a smooth dial. The cold-t pathology (when you include it) is the only regime with a **large, structured** curvature shift.

If you want to test whether the wiggle is “real” vs noise, the next check would be bootstrap or multi-seed bands at each t — my bet is the error bars swallow most of that oscillation except near cold t.

Want me to add a `--gibbs-t-sweep-seeds` option that plots β₂ mean ± band across seeds at each t? That would settle how much is stochastic reshuffling vs signal.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

`frac_var` on the LOO-residual slide is **`frac_var_loo_residual`** — a variance-ratio cousin of $H_{\mathrm{sort}}$, but with LOO as the reference instead of the team mean.

### Definition

On each player-season row:

- **LOO residual:** $r_i = A_i - \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i$
- **Grand total SS:** $\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{grand}} = \sum_i (A_i - \bar{A})^2$

Then:

$$\texttt{frac\_var} = \frac{\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{LOO}}}{\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{grand}}} = \frac{\sum_i (A_i - \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i)^2}{\sum_i (A_i - \bar{A})^2}$$

So it’s: **how much squared “ability minus LOO teammate quality” you have, relative to total ability spread around the grand mean.**

### How to read it (reigning lock ≈ **1.108**)

| Quantity | Team-mean analog | LOO analog |
|----------|------------------|------------|
| Residual | $A_i - \hat{T}_j$ | $A_i - \mathrm{poolq}^{\mathrm{LOO}}_i$ |
| Ratio | $\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{team}}/\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{grand}} \approx 0.936$ | **frac_var ≈ 1.108** |
| Index | $H_{\mathrm{sort}} = 1 - \text{ratio} \approx +0.064$ | $H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{LOO}} = 1 - \text{frac_var} \approx -0.108$ |

**frac_var > 1** means LOO-centered residuals are *bigger* in sum-of-squares than grand-mean demeaning — LOO is not a valid partition of team structure (you’re not subtracting a roster mean that partitions variance). That’s why $H_{\mathrm{sort}}^{\mathrm{LOO}}$ can go **negative**.

### One-liner

> **frac_var** = “fraction of total ability SS left after subtracting LOO” — except it can exceed 1 because LOO isn’t a team partition; it’s a **local congestion** reference, not $\hat{T}_j$.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

That's a fair read of the day — and "reality" is not nothing when the whole thread is **does sim SELECT on frozen rosters reproduce empirical HERO?**

### What actually moved (even without a high-five)

- **Empirical HERO is flat** — that's the anchor. You're not chasing a ghost inverted-U on 09–21 last-ps.
- **Sim at $t_{\mathrm{Gibbs}} \approx 1$ lands in the same flat band** as empirical (617 vs 615 picks, $\beta_2$ near zero). That's a defensible v1 lock for Alex.
- **The $\beta_2$–$t$ wiggle** is a real finding, not a bug: mid-hot $t$ doesn't smoothly tune LOO curvature because **SCORE uses team $L^C$ and HERO reads poolq_LOO**. The dial and the readout aren't on the same axis.
- **Cold Gibbs** is the only regime with a big, structured shape shift — and it's the top-K pathology you already suspected.
- **BDP porch** is richer now: $H_{\mathrm{sort}} \approx 0.06$, LOO vs team residuals, self-inclusion gap — the *why* behind the axis mismatch is documented, not just asserted.

### What felt like dead ends (and kind of were)

- Fine-scanning $t$ hoping for a clean "temperature finds curvature" story — **not there** on this readout.
- Treating $\beta_2$ as a sharp identification statistic — it's noise on a flat object.
- Any fantasy that winsor / overlay / more $t$ points would magically align SCORE and HERO without refitting or changing what's in $S$.

### The honest Alex line from today

> Frozen rosters + reigning MLE score → Gibbs SELECT at $t \approx 1$ reproduces **flat** empirical LOO-HERO at the right draft count. Temperature does **not** cleanly tune curvature on the LOO axis; the main structured failure mode is **cold** (top-K-like). SCORE/HERO axis mismatch is the open sensitivity, not a code error.

That's not a parade — but it's **not** a dead end either. It's the kind of day that stops you from over-claiming in a meeting and points the next real experiment: LOO in SCORE, or accept flat match at $t=1$ and move to outcomes.

If you want a clean stopping point for tonight: you have **one sim HERO overlay PNG**, **one locked $t$**, and **a BDP deck** that explains why team vs LOO matters. That's a full day's reality check.

Want me to drop a short **"Aug 28 — what we learned"** block into the reigning hero README or the MBB replay memo so you don't have to reconstruct this mood tomorrow?

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Congrats on the upgrade — for **this project**, you don’t need to re-tune the repo for “M5 Pro / 48 GB.” Most of what matters is **environment wiring**, not hardware knobs.

### Do these (high priority)

**1. Point Cursor at `sports_net`, not system Python**  
Your global Cursor setting is still:

```json
"python.defaultInterpreterPath": "/usr/bin/python3"
```

That’s **Python 3.9** — not what this repo uses. Switch to:

`/opt/anaconda3/envs/sports_net/bin/python` (3.11.11 — already on the machine)

- **Cursor:** Command Palette → “Python: Select Interpreter” → `sports_net`
- Or add to **workspace** `.vscode/settings.json` (project-only, safer than global):

```json
{
  "python.defaultInterpreterPath": "/opt/anaconda3/envs/sports_net/bin/python",
  "specstory.outputPath": ".specstory/history"
}
```

**2. Fix matplotlib cache (you may hit this on plots)**  
Sandbox run warned `~/.matplotlib` isn’t writable. In `~/.zshrc`:

```bash
export MPLCONFIGDIR="$HOME/.matplotlib"
mkdir -p "$MPLCONFIGDIR"
```

**3. Jupyter notebooks**  
Re-select the **`sports_net`** kernel for `540_tenure_pipeline.ipynb` and any sports notebooks (kernels don’t always carry over on a new Mac).

**4. MCP servers (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`)**  
Paths look fine (`/opt/anaconda3`, `kreuzberg` exists). Just verify:
- **`notebook_mcp`** — local server on `http://127.0.0.1:8080` must be running when you use notebook MCP
- **Brave / Jina** — need `tenure_net`’s `npx` (present)

**5. Rivanna SSH**  
If HPC login fails: copy `~/.ssh/id_*` and `known_hosts` from the old Mac, or regenerate keys and re-add on Rivanna.

**6. PDF conversion**  
If `./scripts/convert_single_md_to_pdf.sh` breaks, reinstall Playwright browsers in `sports_net`:

```bash
conda activate sports_net
playwright install chromium
```

---

### Optional — use the new cores (not required)

Scripts default to **`--n-jobs 8`** (ρ calibration, etc.). On an M5 Pro you can try **12–14** locally; keep headroom for Cursor + Dropbox:

```bash
python sports/scripts/pd21_rho_hsort_calibrate.py --n-jobs 12 ...
```

No repo change needed — just a CLI flag when you want speed.

**48 GB RAM:** no special setting. You’re unlikely to RAM-bound on current MBB porch jobs; Dropbox I/O is still the usual bottleneck.

---

### You do *not* need to change

- Repo paths (Dropbox `CloudStorage` path is fine)
- Git remote / project rules / AGENTS.md
- Rivanna job scripts (those run on HPC, not your laptop)
- Any “M5-specific” Cursor flags — there aren’t meaningful ones for your workflow

### What I ran
```bash

git reset HEAD~1
```

That **removes the commit** and **unstages everything**, but **keeps your file changes** in the working tree (unstaged).

**Now:** HEAD is at **`82339df`** · **0 files staged**

---

### For next time (cheat sheet)

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| **Undo commit + unstage, keep files** | `git reset HEAD~1` |
| **Undo commit, keep files staged** | `git reset --soft HEAD~1` |
| **Undo commit AND discard all those changes** | `git reset --hard HEAD~1` ⚠️ |
| **Only unstage (no commit undo)** | `git restore --staged .` |

---

### Important on new Mac + Dropbox
**Don’t keep `.git` in Dropbox-synced folders** if you can avoid it — branch refs get conflict copies and git breaks.

Options:
1. Move repo out of Dropbox (clone to `~/Projects/...`)
2. Or pause Dropbox while committing
3. Or use git only on one machine + push/pull via GitHub

If you want, I can help you **re-stage only specific files** (e.g. skip giant `.specstory` diffs) before the next commit.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

In **zsh**, `#` only starts a comment in interactive shells if you turn that on:

```bash
setopt interactivecomments
```

Then this works:

```bash
git log -1 --oneline    # should show 82339df
```

To keep it every session, add that line to `~/.zshrc`.

**Without that option:** zsh treats `#` as a normal character in pasted one-liners, so either:
- run commands **without** the comment part, or
- put comments on their own line in a script (`#!/bin/zsh` files always allow `#` comments).

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**Git and rsync do different jobs.** After `git push` / `git pull`, use rsync only for the big gitignored trees.

Canonical reference: [`scripts/DATA_SYNC.md`](scripts/DATA_SYNC.md)

---

## Split of responsibility

| Layer | Tool | What moves |
|-------|------|------------|
| Code, docs, tracked JSON/PNG | **`git pull` / `git push`** | Everything *not* in `.gitignore` |
| Large generated data | **rsync scripts** | Everything *in* `.gitignore` that you still need on both sides |

You do **not** rsync the whole repo to “sync Ivy_Net.” You rsync **specific subtrees**.

---

## Scripts (what to use when)

| Script | Direction | Use for |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| **`rsync_push_to_hpc.sh`** | Mac → Rivanna | Code / small files **up** (won’t overwrite HPC-generated blobs) |
| **`rsync_pull_from_hpc.sh`** | Rivanna → Mac | One subtree **down** |
| **`rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh`** | Rivanna → Mac | **One-shot** refresh (logs + sweep + optional tenure) |
| **`rsync_hpc_include.sh`** | (shared config) | Excludes — not run directly |

Overrides if needed: `HPC_USER`, `HPC_HOST`, `HPC_REPO` (default `~/Ivy_Net` on Rivanna).

---

## Big `.gitignore` areas → which rsync

| Data (gitignored) | Typical path | Mac → HPC | HPC → Mac |
|-------------------|--------------|-----------|-----------|
| **MBB bulk CSV/SQLite** | `datasets/mbb/**` | Manual / rare | Manual / rare — **not** in default rsync |
| **Sports panel copies** | `sports/datasets/mbb/*` | Same | Same |
| **Tenure pipeline outputs** | `tenure/tenure_pipeline/*.jsonl`, OA cache, PNGs | `rsync_push_to_hpc.sh tenure/tenure_pipeline` (code only; excludes protect big files) | `rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh tenure` or `rsync_pull_from_hpc.sh tenure/tenure_pipeline` |
| **Slurm logs** | `slurm_out/` | Rarely | `rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh logs` or `quick` |
| **537/538 sweep results** | `sports/outputs/simulation_sweeps/rivanna_faithful_*` | Push **scripts** only: `rsync_push_to_hpc.sh sweep` | `rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh sweep` or `quick` |
| **Faculty HTML snapshots** | `**/faculty_snapshots/` | **No** (HPC-only) | **No** (excluded on purpose) |
| **DBLP parsed / XML** | `tenure/.../dblp_parsed/`, `dblp.xml` | N/A | **No** in normal pull — copy manually if needed |
| **`python_packages/`** | whole tree | Usually Git isn’t used; push subtree if you customize | Rare |

**Tracked exception (use Git, not rsync):** `datasets/mbb/empirical_perf_fit.json` — see `datasets/mbb/README_TRACKED_ARTIFACTS.md`.

---

## Usual workflows

**After you pushed code (what you just did):**

On **Rivanna** — code only:

```bash
cd ~/Ivy_Net
git pull origin main
```

No rsync needed for the commit you just pushed.

**Rivanna ran jobs → you want outputs on Mac (Cursor):**

```bash
# Slurm logs + 537/538 sweep only (light)
./scripts/rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh quick

# + tenure pipeline JSONL/PNG/cache
./scripts/rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh all
```

**Mac code changes → Rivanna (without clobbering HPC data):**

```bash
./scripts/rsync_push_to_hpc.sh all
# or targeted: tenure/tenure_pipeline, sweep, etc.
```

**MBB / reigning-hero work:** Your new commit is mostly **tracked** sandbox outputs under `3-Master_Plan/...` and scripts — that’s **Git**, not rsync. Rsync matters when you run heavy sims on Rivanna and need `slurm_out/` or `rivanna_faithful_*` locally.

---

## Why Cursor still shows lots of CHANGES

That’s almost certainly **uncommitted** stuff left after your selective commit, for example:

- `09_21` hero/fhero files you didn’t `git add`
- `_archive/`, `docs/n.docx`, `run_sr_rescrape*`
- Modified `.specstory` / `wallst/history.csv` if you didn’t `git restore` them
- New untracked `.specstory` chat files

Run `git status -sb | wc -l` — if you see many `??` and ` M`, that’s normal; it’s **not** fixed by rsync.

---

**Short answer:** Use **`git pull`/`git push`** for the repo; use **`rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh`** (usually `quick` or `all`) to pull big gitignored outputs **from Rivanna to Mac**, and **`rsync_push_to_hpc.sh`** to push code **Mac → Rivanna** without overwriting HPC-generated data. You don’t need rsync to “finish” today’s git push unless you also need Slurm logs, sweep trees, or tenure pipeline blobs on the other machine.

## 2. Dropbox "offline" on the old Mac

**"Make available offline"** is per-machine: it tells Dropbox to keep a full local copy *on that Mac*. It does **not** export a manifest to a new Mac. Migration Assistant moves user files/apps; it does **not** replicate Dropbox's cloud selective-sync / offline cache state.

On the new Mac, Dropbox re-syncs from the cloud. Files that were only partially synced (or mid-conflict when `.git` got corrupted) can show up late or as `*conflicted copy*`. That matches what happened — not a git failure.

**SpecStory cloud** is separate from Dropbox: login + "Sync with Cloud" in the extension covers chats even if Dropbox lagged. **Git commit of `.specstory/history/`** is your durable backup for Rivanna and history in the repo.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

You're not missing something obvious — git has **three different buckets**, and Cursor's CHANGES panel mixes two of them. **Gitignored stuff is a third bucket Cursor usually doesn't show at all.**

---

## Three buckets (simple)

Think of your project folder like a office with three filing systems:

### 1. **In git and saved on GitHub** (committed)
Git knows about these files. GitHub has the same version you last pushed.

Your SpecStory chat files from today are **here now**. Push worked. You're good.

### 2. **Git sees them, but they're not saved in git yet** (what CHANGES shows)
These are **not** gitignored. Git is deliberately telling you: *"These files exist on your Mac, and they're different from (or missing from) what's in the repo."*

Two flavors:

| What Cursor/git says | Plain English |
|----------------------|---------------|
| **`M` (modified)** | File is **already in git**, but you edited it on disk since the last commit. |
| **`??` (untracked)** | File is **on your Mac**, git **never committed it**, but nothing in `.gitignore` hides it. |

Right now you have roughly:
- **3 modified** — tenure docs (and similar)
- **~357 untracked** — mostly HERO/FHERO PNGs and JSONs in `population_sandbox/`

**Why does Cursor bother you?** Because these files **could** be committed. Cursor is a todo list: *"You might want to save these to GitHub too."* It's not saying they're ignored — it's the opposite.

### 3. **Gitignore — git pretends they don't exist** (usually invisible in CHANGES)
Examples in your repo: `datasets/mbb/**`, huge tenure `.jsonl` files, `slurm-*.out`.

Git **does not list these** in `git status`. Cursor **usually doesn't show them** either. They're "local / too big / reproducible — don't put in GitHub."

So: **no, the 357 lines are not gitignore alerts.** If they were gitignored, you wouldn't see them.

---

## What happened today (timeline)

1. **Before** — Hundreds of files were **staged** (marked "include in next commit") but not committed. That made CHANGES huge and scary.
2. **You committed SpecStory** — Those chat files moved to bucket 1 (on GitHub).
3. **Sync failed** — Not because of gitignore. Because **Sync = pull + push**, and pull-with-rebase wants a **clean** bucket 2 for the files git already tracks. You still had a few **modified** files (tenure docs, etc.), so git said no.
4. **Push alone worked** — You only needed to upload; you weren't behind GitHub.

---

## Modified vs untracked (why both show up)

**Modified (`M`):**  
Like a chapter already in the published dissertation, but you edited the Word file on your desk. Git says: *"The saved version and your desk version differ."*

**Untracked (`??`):**  
Like a new folder of plots you generated yesterday. Git says: *"I see these on your machine; you never told me to track them."*

Neither means "error." Neither means "Dropbox broke git." They mean: **local work exists that isn't on GitHub yet** (and might never need to be).

---

## "Stage all" vs what you want

- **Commit** = save a snapshot **into git on your Mac**.
- **Push** = copy those snapshots **to GitHub**.
- **Stage** = check off which files go into the **next** commit.

**Stage all** checks off **everything** Cursor shows — including 357 plot files you probably don't want on GitHub.

That's why we said: stage **only SpecStory** this time, not everything.

---

## What you can do with what's left (~360 lines)

Pick one attitude — all are valid:

| You want… | Do… |
|-----------|-----|
| **Ignore for now** | Nothing. Files stay on your Mac. CHANGES stays noisy. Harmless. |
| **Stop seeing the plot files** | Add paths to `.gitignore` (we can do that together). They disappear from CHANGES. |
| **Save plots to GitHub too** | Stage those folders and commit (big commit — like today's accident). |
| **Drop the 3 tenure edits** | `git restore` those files → back to last committed version. |

---

## One-sentence summary

**CHANGES is a list of "stuff on your Mac that git could save but hasn't (or that's edited since last save)" — not a list of gitignored files, and not proof anything is broken.**

Your SpecStory work **is** on GitHub now. The rest is optional local/science output Cursor is offering you for a future commit.

If you want the panel quiet for normal "stage all" workflow, the next step is deciding: **gitignore the sweep outputs**, or **commit them on purpose in one science commit**. Say which you prefer and we can do it step by step in Cursor. After that, we can talk `.git` in Dropbox in the same plain language.

Your intent is right. Git + SpecStory **do** support “Mac Cursor sometimes, Rivanna Cursor when I need HPC.” The problem today wasn’t that plan — it was **Dropbox also trying to sync the `.git` folder**, which is git’s private database.

---

## What you’re trying to do (and it’s valid)

| Layer | Job | Mac | Rivanna |
|-------|-----|-----|---------|
| **Git / GitHub** | Code, notebooks, docs, `.specstory/history/`, tracked small outputs | Edit → commit → push | `git pull` → work → (optional) commit → push |
| **SpecStory cloud** | Chat history searchable across machines | Auto-saves + cloud sync | Same extension + login when tunneled in |
| **rsync** | Big tenure panels, Slurm logs, gitignored blobs | Pull from HPC for local Cursor | Lives on HPC; generated there |
| **Dropbox** | Dissertation docs, convenience backup | Your current workspace path | Usually **not** involved |

You already proved the git layer works: Mac pushed → Rivanna `git pull` → `0d1802a`. That **is** the Mac ↔ Rivanna sync for everything not in `.gitignore`.

---

## What `.git` is (one sentence)

The `.git` folder is **git’s filing cabinet** — commits, branches, history. It is **not** your project files. GitHub holds a copy; your Mac and Rivanna each have a local copy. **`git push` / `git pull` move work between them.**

---

## Why `.git` in Dropbox is a bad mix

Dropbox syncs **every file** in the folder, including `.git/`.

So you had **two sync systems** on the same hidden database:

- Git writing `refs/heads/main` during commit/push  
- Dropbox rewriting or duplicating files → `*conflicted copy*`, broken refs, timeouts  

That caused today’s mess. **Your workflow doesn’t require Dropbox to sync `.git`.** GitHub already does that.

**Dropbox for dissertation files:** fine.  
**Dropbox syncing `.git`:** high risk, zero benefit if you use GitHub.

---

## A simple mental model (three lanes)

```
Lane 1 — GIT (GitHub)     code, docs, SpecStory markdown, tracked plots/scripts
         Mac  ←——→  GitHub  ←——→  Rivanna

Lane 2 — RSYNC            huge tenure JSONL, slurm_out, faculty_snapshots, datasets/mbb bulk
         Mac  ←——  Rivanna only (see scripts/DATA_SYNC.md)

Lane 3 — SPECSTORY CLOUD  chat UI/history (optional backup to Lane 1 via committed .md files)
         Mac  ←——→  cloud  ←——→  Rivanna (when logged in)
```

Dropbox is a **fourth lane** that overlaps Lane 1’s folder on your Mac. That overlap is what hurt you.

---

## Practical setup for your Mac + Rivanna Cursor habit

### Rivanna (you’re already doing this)

```bash
cd ~/Ivy_Net
git pull origin main    # start of session
# ... Cursor over tunnel, Slurm, tenure work ...
git push origin main    # only if you committed something on HPC
```

Big tenure data: stays on HPC. Pull logs/panels to Mac with `./scripts/rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh` when you want local Cursor to read them.

### Mac — two options

**Option A — recommended long term:**  
Clone/work in **`~/Projects/Ivy_Net`** (or anywhere **not** in Dropbox). Dissertation Word/PDF stays in Dropbox; code repo uses **Lane 1 only**.

**Option B — keep opening the Dropbox path in Cursor:**  
Usable if you accept guardrails:

- Don’t edit the same repo on two Macs at once  
- Pause Dropbox before heavy git ops if things get weird  
- **Never** treat Dropbox as git backup — GitHub is canonical  
- Re-run `find .git -name '*conflicted copy*'` after Dropbox glitches  

Option A removes a whole class of failures; Option B is “I know the risk.”

### SpecStory on both machines

- **Committed `.specstory/history/`** → Rivanna gets it via `git pull` (you did this today).  
- **SpecStory cloud** → same chats in the UI on Mac and Rivanna without relying on Dropbox.  
- Two backups of conversations: git (durable, in repo) + cloud (convenient).

---

## Typical week with your intent

1. **Mac:** Cursor on Ivy_Net → edit → commit → `git push`.  
2. **Rivanna:** SSH tunnel → Cursor on `~/Ivy_Net` → `git pull` → run reconciliation / Slurm.  
3. **Back on Mac:** `rsync_pull_recent_hpc.sh` if you need Slurm logs or tenure panels locally.  
4. **Git again** only for code/doc changes — not for multi-GB JSONL (that’s rsync + `.gitignore`).

---

## Direct answers

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| Was git the wrong tool for Mac + Rivanna Cursor? | **No.** GitHub + pull/push is exactly right. |
| Was SpecStory the wrong tool? | **No.** Git + cloud fits your setup. |
| What went wrong? | **Dropbox syncing `.git`**, plus one scary recovery day — not your normal workflow. |
| Do I need Dropbox for Mac ↔ Rivanna code sync? | **No.** GitHub handles that. |
| Can I keep the repo in Dropbox? | **You can**, but moving `.git` out of Dropbox’s reach (move the whole clone) is the clean fix. |

## What actually went wrong

It wasn’t “Charles uses two Macs on Ivy_Net daily.” It was:

**Old Mac + new Mac + Dropbox still moving terabytes + `.git` in the same tree**

For a while, Dropbox was effectively **two writers** on one repo:

- Old machine still had state (including refs pointing at the bad commit)
- New machine was working before sync finished
- `.git` files got conflict copies and half-updated refs

That’s a **migration edge case**, not your normal habit. With one Mac and settled Dropbox, your track record suggests this stays rare.

---

## Your normal workflow is fine

| Your practice | Risk |
|---------------|------|
| One Mac at a time for the repo | Low |
| GitHub as publish step (push / pull on Rivanna) | Correct |
| SpecStory + git for Mac ↔ HPC | Correct |
| Repo in Dropbox for dissertation proximity | Usually OK **once migration is done** |

I was steering you toward `~/Projects/Ivy_Net` as the **safest** long-term layout — not because you’re doing something wrong day to day, but because migration proved how ugly it gets when Dropbox and git overlap during a big sync.

**Staying in the Dropbox path is a reasonable choice** if migration is finished and you’re on one Mac again.

---

## Lightweight guardrails (no repo move required)

**1. Migration is “done” when Dropbox says so**  
On the new Mac: Dropbox fully synced, no “Syncing…” on the repo folder, no `*conflicted copy*` under `.git` or the tree.

**2. After any big Dropbox event** (new Mac, restore, huge folder move):

```bash
find .git -name '*conflicted copy*'
```

Empty output = good.

**3. Git sync = GitHub, not Dropbox**  
Mac commits and pushes → Rivanna pulls. You already do this.

**4. If git acts weird and Dropbox was recently busy**  
Pause Dropbox for a minute, retry the git command. Today’s timeouts fit that pattern.

**5. Rivanna unchanged**  
`~/Ivy_Net`, `git pull` at session start. No Dropbox involved there.

---

## Bottom line

You don’t have a chronic “two Macs + Dropbox + git” problem. You had a **one-time migration storm** that mimicked that. Your intent (Mac Cursor, Rivanna Cursor, git + SpecStory, rsync for big tenure data) is sound.

Moving the clone out of Dropbox is **optional hardening**, not a verdict on how you’ve been working. Staying put is fine once sync has settled — just remember **GitHub carries the repo; Dropbox carries the folder.**

If anything still feels off on the new Mac (Dropbox stuck, CHANGES exploding again), say what you see and we can triage. Otherwise you’re good to go on Rivanna tenure work.

**To Alex — where we are on the Wang arc (MBB) and next step on tenure**

Alex,

Quick status before Charles and PEER go heads-down on tenure scraping.

**Where we are on the paper (Wang progression, MBB)**

We’re in the middle of the Wang ladder on basketball — **regularity → minimal model → testable predictions** — with the three layers kept separate (environment vs **score → select**).

**Empirical (Pass A).** On the cleaned NCAA panel we have stable **HERO** readouts (draft rate vs LOO teammate quality) and **F-HERO** (draft rate vs team-mean performance at fixed Â). The canonical story is locked: LOO hero is **flat at the elite end** on the post-QC panel (mg10); F-HERO on T̂_j is a **different object** with its own shape. Provenance strips, sandbox CLI, and population sweeps (windows, ALLT vs +DFT, permutation matrix, etc.) are in the repo under `population_sandbox/`.

**Generative (MBB — your PD28 “porch” move).** We **parked homophily** for basketball (ρ\* ≈ 0, H_sort bracket flat). The active MBB program is **empirical rosters frozen → fit γ\*, λ\*, temperature → simulate draftees → replay HERO**. That chain is **done on the reigning 2009–21 aperture** (min20, mg10): calibration JSONs, Gibbs SELECT sweep, and **sim-vs-empirical HERO replay** (`reigning_hero/`). So MBB is not “still hunting for ρ”; it’s “does **select** on real locker rooms reproduce the empirical hero **shape family**?”

**Open on MBB (not blocking tenure).** Sensitivity bands, tighter sim/emp axis alignment, optional F-HERO dual readout, and a few population sweeps you asked about (e.g. 13–21 vs 11–21) — queued, not forgotten.

**What we’re doing now**

You’d like **HERO / F-HERO-style metrics on tenure** — same readout machinery, new domain. The tenure panel is **not yet at the same robustness as MBB** for that exploration. Charles and **PEER** are spending the next stretch on **scraping and adjudication** (more schools/URLs, cleaner faculty snapshots, panel rebuild on Rivanna) so the tenure side is worth plotting.

**After the tenure dataset is stronger — what to hand COMPASS (planning agent) so Charles can move fast**

When you and Charles are happy with the scrape/panel, a **short lock memo** (even bullet points) with:

1. **Outcome Y** — What is “success”? (e.g. tenure granted, promotion to associate, time-to-tenure event.) Person-year vs absorbing state.
2. **Panel aperture** — Which years, which institutions (R1 CS only? expanded list?), minimum activity filters (MBB analog of min20/mg10).
3. **Ability Â** — Which productivity field(s) for the talent axis and for F-HERO-style “fixed Â” slices (OpenAlex? DBLP? pre-tenure window only?).
