Alex’s drive-by fixes are in — refreshed mosaic at `3-Master_Plan/re_entry/HEROs_and_PASSes/sports_sandbox/data_story/MBB_DATA_STORY_reigning_3x3.png`. Point-by-point:

---

### 1 · Title says 09–21; panels 7–8 are 11–21 — did we decide 09–21 would be worse?

**No — we never locked “09–21 is worse.”** We chose **11–21 +DFT** for row 3 because the signal reads **cleaner**, not because 09–21 fails.

I re-ran both windows for comparison (`data_story/_compare_0921/`):

| Panel | 11–21 +DFT (in deck) | 09–21 +DFT |
|--------|----------------------|------------|
| **7 · CCT P1** | Squid **38.8%** vs Jackal **25.3%** (CCT=YES, n=425) | Squid **35.0%** vs Jackal **28.0%** (CCT=YES, n=534) |
| **8 · Elite pond** | Plateau **25.4%** → tail **14.1%** | Plateau **25.9%** → tail **17.4%** |

So **09–21 still shows more Squids drafted than Jackals** — your insight holds — but the Squid–Jackal **gap is wider** in 11–21. Elite-tail downturn is visible in both; 11–21 is a bit sharper.

**Deck choice:** Title/cohort stay **09–21 reigning** (panels 1–6, 9). Cohort cell now footnotes **“Panels 7–8: 2011–21 +DFT (CCT / elite pond screening).”** Happy to swap row 3 to 09–21 if you want full window alignment — say the word.

---

### 2 · Plot 3a — winsor removed ✓

Panel 3 now uses `...poolq_loo_dist_..._nowinsor.png` (raw LOO tails, no 1–99 clip).

---

### 3 · What does plot 3b tell us?

**3b is the ECDF (cumulative distribution)** of the same LOO variable as 3a:

- **Blue** = all last-ps players  
- **Purple +DFT** = players on rosters with any ever-drafted teammate  

If +DFT sits **above and to the left** of the full curve, draftees systematically come from **better peer ponds** — at every LOO level, a larger share of drafted-context players are already “high pond.” That’s a **descriptive sorting fact** about who gets drafted, *before* we bin draft *rates* (HERO/CCT). It motivates “environment matters” without being the hero curve itself.

---

### 4 · Plot 5a — layout + sort-and-chop ✓

- Legend → **upper left** (off the right-tail peak)  
- Stats box → **upper right**, two lines  
- **Crimson sort-and-chop dashed line removed** — agree there’s no deck reason to keep it; it was a PD21 ρ benchmark, not part of the MBB story.

---

### 5 · Plot 9 — EW midpoint x-labels ✓

Plot 9 (HERO EW16) now labels x-ticks with **poolq_LOO bin midpoints**; **n** stays on the bars. Plot 8 (PW 4+7 piecewise bins) stays **bin index** — midpoints would mislead when bin widths differ.

---

### 6 · Plots 7–9 — less aggressive title/footer wrap ✓

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Investigating the text stepping issue at the bottom of plots 7 and 8.

The footer text sits in figure coordinates while the xlabel sits in axes coordinates. With `bbox_inches="tight"`, these elements overlap at the bottom. The 16 x-axis ticks in panel 7 add further crowding.

Panel 8 likely has a longer footer text that worsens the crowding. I am weighing several fixes: dynamically adjusting the bottom margin based on line count, moving the footer higher in figure coordinates, collapsing the footer into fewer lines, or removing `bbox_inches="tight"` since `subplots_adjust` already handles spacing.

The bottom margin is too small for the stacked footer lines. Panel 7 has sixteen x-axis bins and panel 8 has eleven. I will increase the default bottom margin in `layout_bar_figure` for CCT plots that include footers.

A concrete implementation is taking shape. `stamp_wrapped_footer` will accept a line-height parameter and return the number of wrapped lines. `layout_bar_figure` will then scale the bottom margin upward based on that count. This removes the need for `bbox_inches="tight"` and prevents the footer from overlapping the axis labels.

Panel 7 needs its bottom margin raised to 0.28 or 0.30, with the footer placed at y=0.04 using explicit line-by-line coordinates. X-axis tick rotation may also be needed for panel 7.

Panel 5a still has a layout problem. The coverage curve peaks on the right side, so placing the stats box in the upper right corner obscures that tail peak. The legend in the upper left also continues to hide data.

Panel 5a needs its legend moved to the lower left where coverage is low. The stats box should shift to the lower right or sit below the plot entirely. Using `fig.legend` or `bbox_to_anchor` would place the legend outside the axes. The current upper-right stats box blocks the curve's right-side peak.

The stats box will move to the lower right at (0.98, 0.05). The legend will move to the lower left at (0.02, 0.05). Coverage curves typically peak in the upper area, so the lower corners avoid obscuring the tail. A single horizontal row below the title is another option.

The 2×2 grid leaves little room for legends placed outside the axes. The stats box will shrink to two lines and sit at the bottom-right. The legend will move to the bottom-left. Both will stay in the lower coverage region. I am also checking whether the mosaic builder crops panels. The `stamp_wrapped_footer` helper is being rewritten to accept a `line_spacing` argument.

The footer helper now stacks lines from bottom to top using reversed iteration. `layout_bar_figure` will accept a `footer_lines` argument and raise the bottom margin by roughly 0.018 per line. The sequence is: stamp the footer first, then call `layout_bar_figure` with the returned line count so the bottom margin adjusts automatically.

Panel 8 hardcodes bottom=0.24, which may still be too small once the footer is stamped. The main culprit is `bbox_inches='tight'` in `savefig`; it rescales the figure and often overrides `subplots_adjust`, causing the footer and xlabel to collide. Removing that flag for bar charts with footers should fix the overlap.

The empirical team-interval plot will keep `bbox_inches='tight'` because its layout will be fixed inside `subplots_adjust`. The plan is to update `hero_plot_style` first, then apply the new footer helper and higher bottom margin to `plot_matched_pond`
</details></think>

Plot 5a will lose its legend box. The legend labels will become a subtitle line in the plot title instead. This avoids the panel edge cutoff.

Plots 7 and 8 still need their bottom margins tightened. The current gap between the x-axis note and the bottom text rows is too large.

The footer is currently anchored at figure coordinates near y=0.01, while the axes bottom sits near y=0.15. This mismatch creates the large gap. I will update the footer function to place text just below the axes using the actual bottom margin.

The root cause of the footer gaps in plots 7, 8, and 9 is now clear. The footer is currently anchored at figure coordinates near y=0.01, while the axes bottom sits near y=0.15. This mismatch leaves a large empty space between the x-axis note and the bottom text rows.

The fix is to call `fig.subplots_adjust()` first, then read the actual bottom margin via `fig.subplotpars.bottom`. The footer will be placed just below the axes using that real coordinate instead of a fixed figure coordinate. This should eliminate the gap in plots 7, 8, and 9.

Plot 9 shares the same footer placement bug, so it will benefit from the same correction. The footer lines may also need slight spacing adjustments to prevent stepping onto the bottom text.

I am rewriting `layout_bar_figure` to return the computed bottom margin. `stamp_wrapped_footer` will accept that value directly, falling back to `fig.subplotpars.bottom` when it is omitted. This ties the footer position to the actual axes bottom rather than a fixed figure coordinate.

The footer will sit just below the x-axis at `axes_bottom - 0.006`, with each line spaced downward by `line_spacing`. The layout function must run first so `subplotpars.bottom` is known, then the footer is stamped with that exact bottom margin passed in.

A single `finalize_bar_figure` function will replace the separate layout and footer steps. It wraps footer lines, adds bottom padding for rotated x-axes, and stamps the text at the correct y-coordinate in one pass.

The finalized footer will sit at `fig.subplotpars.bottom - 0.004` with 0.012 line spacing. For Plot 5a, the legend will be removed entirely and replaced by a title subtitle that reads "Blue fill = actual rosters · gray dashed = no overlap ($=1$)".

import pandas as pd
from pass_a_congestion_conditional import CctSpec, _get_panel

def band_stats(season_min, season_max, dft, panel_rows=&#39;last-ps&#39;):
    base = CctSpec(
        season_min=season_min, season_max=season_max,
        min_minutes=20.0, min_team_season_games=10,
        winsor_lo=0.01, winsor_hi=0.99, n_bins=16,
        ai_lo=None, ai_hi=None, perf_metric=&#39;ppm&#39;,
        dft=dft, y_draft_mode=&#39;ever&#39;, panel_rows=panel_rows,
    )
    use = _get_panel(base).dropna(subset=[&#39;perf&#39;,&#39;Y_draft&#39;])

    top7 = perf &gt;= np.quantile(perf, 0.93)
    z7_cut = float(np.quantile(perf, 0.93))
    z2_cut = 2.0
    z3_cut = 3.0
    # also report as &#39;above z=2&#39; share
    above2 = perf &gt;= 2.0
    above3 = perf &gt;= 3.0
    print(f&#39;=== {season_min}-{season_max} dft={dft} panel_rows={panel_rows} n={n:,} ===&#39;)
    print(f&#39;  z in [2,3]: {in23.sum():,} ({100*in23.mean:.2f}% of panel)&#39;)
    print(f&#39;  z &gt;= 2:     {above2.sum():,} ({100*above2.mean:.2f}%)&#39;)
    print(f&#39;  z &gt;= 3:     {above3.sum():,} ({100*above3.mean:.2f}%)&#39;)
    print(f&#39;  top 7%:     {top7.sum():,} ({100*top7.mean:.2f}%) · cut z&gt;={z7_cut:.3f}&#39;)
    print(f&#39;  overlap [2,3] &amp; top7: {((in23)&amp;(top7)).sum()}&#39;)
    print()

for args in [

## 1. What % is z ∈ [2, 3] vs top 7%?

These are **different gates** — not “ventile 2–3” vs “ventile top.”

| **Panel 8** | **Top 7%** Â (pooled percentile cut) | **1,237 rows (7.0%)** · z ≥ **1.49** | 1,596 rows (7.0%) · z ≥ **1.65** |

Important nuance: **everyone in z ∈ [2, 3] is inside top 7%** (overlap is 100%). Panel 7 is the **narrower, higher-Â slice**:

- Panel 8: “elite” ≈ top 7% (z ≳ 1.5–1.7)
- Panel 7: “very elite but capped” ≈ top **~2.4–3%**, excluding z > 3 (~0.3% above the ceiling)

So “good but not max ventile” in `plot_highlights` is imprecise. Better:

- **Panel 7:** fixed **z window** [2, 3] — upper tail, **not** the whole top 7%; “not max” = **z capped at 3**, not “mid ventiles.”

import json
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.image as mpimg

REPO = Path('.')
OUT = REPO / '3-Master_Plan/re_entry/HEROs_and_PASSes/sports_sandbox/data_story/_compare_0921'

def side_by_side(left: Path, right: Path, out: Path, *, suptitle: str, left_title: str, right_title: str, dpi=200):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(22, 6.2))
    for ax, path, title in zip(axes, [left, right], [left_title, right_title], strict=True):
        img = mpimg.imread(path)
        ax.imshow(img, aspect='auto')
        ax.axis('off')
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=12, pad=8, fontweight='bold')
    fig.suptitle(suptitle, fontsize=13, y=0.98)
    fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.90, wspace=0.02, left=0.01, right=0.99, bottom=0.02)
    fig.savefig(out, dpi=dpi, facecolor='white')
    plt.close(fig)
    print('Wrote', out)

# Panel 7 stats from JSON
j7_9 = json.loads((OUT / 'CCT_draft_rate_ai_band_poolq_loo_min20_ppm_z2_3_dft.json').read_text())

j7_11 = json.loads(j7_11_path.read_text())

def cct_line(j):
    s, k = j['squid_proxy'], j['jackal_proxy']
    return (f"Squid {100*s['draft_rate']:.1f}% vs Jackal {100*k['draft_rate']:.1f}% · "
            f"CCT={'YES' if j['cct_signature_squid_gt_jackal'] else 'NO'} · band n={j['band_n']:,}")

side_by_side(
    OUT / 'CCT_draft_rate_ai_band_poolq_loo_min20_ppm_z2_3_dft_9_21.png',
    OUT / 'CCT_draft_rate_ai_band_poolq_loo_min20_ppm_z2_3_dft_11_21.png',
    OUT / 'COMPARE_panel7_CCT_z23_9_21_vs_11_21.png',
    suptitle='Panel 7 · CCT PPM z ∈ [2, 3] · +DFT · QTL16 · matched Â band',
    left_title=f"2009–2021\n{cct_line(j7_9)}",
    right_title=f"2011–2021 (deck)\n{cct_line(j7_11)}",
)

        return f"band n={prov.get('n_rows', '?'):,} · drafts={prov.get('n_drafts', '?')}"
    return (f"plateau {100*knee.get('plateau_mean_draft_rate', knee.get('plateau', 0)):.1f}% → "
            f"tail {100*knee.get('tail_mean_draft_rate', knee.get('tail', 0)):.1f}% · "
            f"downturn={'YES' if knee.get('alex_downturn_visible', knee.get('downturn')) else 'NO'}")

### What we have

| **Gap vs MBB** | **No tenure CCT / elite-pond analog yet** (Act II F-HERO still pending) |

So we can ship a **v1 screening deck** now; row 3 won’t mirror MBB panels 7–8 until we build fixed-Â conditional plots (or we use PD29 substitutes).

### Proposed tenure 3×3 (PD29 reigning)

Read TL → BR, parallel to MBB:

| | Col 1 | Col 2 | Col 3 |
|--|--------|--------|--------|
| **R1** | **1 · Cohort** (text: decision-year, infHM resolved, N=389) | **2 · Own Â + dept T̂** (`TENURE_pubs_career_rate_pd29` or mean-by-outcome) | **3 · Dept LOO dist** (`TENURE_poolq_loo_distribution_infHM` or PD29 dept LOO rate) |
| **R2** | **4 · “Mass” story** (`TENURE_pubs_career_rate_by_outcome_pd29` — where tenure mass lives) | **5 · Overlap** (`TENURE_pool_interval_overlap_infHM`) | **6 · Pond size** (`TENURE_pool_size_loo_distribution_infHM`) |
| **R3** | **7 · TBD** (placeholder or fixed-Â slice when built) | **8 · Decision timing** (`TENURE_decision_asst_time_exit_pd29`) | **9 · HERO** (`HERO_tenure_q16_decision_dept_loo_infHM_slide.png`) |

Panel 9 should use the **`_slide.png`** variant if we want MBB-matched styling (LPM badge, cleaner footer).

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Yes — the current format is the weakest link in the PD29 porch. Plain single-panel histograms (especially **overlapping** tenured vs attrition) read poorly at N≈389.

### What’s wrong now
- **32-bin histogram** on a narrow range → choppy bars, no smooth read
- **Overlapping hists** → muddy middle, hard to compare medians
- **Raw career-pubs rate** (0–9) → less intuitive than a standardized peer-environment scale
- **No cumulative view** → can’t see “draftees shift left/right” the way MBB panel 3b does

### Better formats (ranked)

| Format | Best for | Why |
|--------|----------|-----|
| **1. MBB mirror: hist + ECDF** | `dept_loo_career_rate_pd29` | Same as MBB panel 3 — left = support, right = ECDF + median line + stats box. Deck-native. |
| **2. Dual ECDF by outcome** | `dept_loo_by_outcome_pd29` | Tenured vs attrition as **two step curves** (not overlapping bars). Cleanest comparison at this N. |
| **3. Ridgeline or small multiples** | By-outcome | Two aligned density/hist panels, shared x-axis — no overlap mud. |
| **4. Box/violin by outcome** | Quick median shift | Compact; good for slides, less “story” than ECDF. |
| **5. Z-scored x** (optional overlay) | Both | Express dept LOO as **within-cohort z** so the x-axis reads like MBB poolq_LOO (“peer environment relative to cohort”). |

### Recommendation for the tenure 3×3
- **Panel 3 (peer context):** **hist + ECDF** (option 1), optionally with x as cohort z-score  
- **Substitute for overlapping hist:** **dual ECDF** (option 2) or ridgeline (option 3)

The **career_rate_by_outcome** plot has the same overlapping-hist issue; the same ECDF fix applies there if you want consistency.

import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
REPO = Path('.').resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO/'tenure'/'tenure_pipeline'))
from decision_year_cohort import build_decision_cohort_records
panel = REPO/'tenure/tenure_pipeline/faculty_panel_with_pools.jsonl'
career = REPO/'tenure/tenure_pipeline/author_year_career_master.jsonl'
recs, stats = build_decision_cohort_records(panel, career)
df = pd.DataFrame(recs)
work = df.dropna(subset=['pubs_per_career_year']).copy()
# z within decision year
work['z'] = work.groupby('decision_year')['pubs_per_career_year'].transform(lambda s: (s-s.mean())/s.std() if s.std()>0 else 0)
# also pooled z
mu, sd = work['pubs_per_career_year'].mean(), work['pubs_per_career_year'].std()
work['z_pooled'] = (work['pubs_per_career_year']-mu)/sd
for label, col in [('within-year z','z'), ('pooled z','z_pooled')]:
    top7 = work.nlargest(max(1,int(round(0.07*len(work)))), 'pubs_per_career_year')
    band23 = work[(work[col]>=2)&(work[col]<=3)]
    print(label, 'N=', len(work), 'top7%=', len(top7), f\"({100*len(top7)/len(work):.1f}%)\", 'z[2,3]=', len(band23), f\"({100*len(band23)/len(work):.1f}%)\")
# hero persons with loo
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO/'tenure'/'tenure_pipeline'))
from decision_hero_prep import prepare_decision_hero_persons
persons, _ = prepare_decision_hero_persons(panel, career)
pdf = pd.DataFrame(persons)
merged = work.merge(pdf[['faculty_id','dept_loo_career_rate']], on='faculty_id', how='inner')
print('with both A and LOO:', len(merged), 'top7% with LOO:', int(round(0.07*len(merged))))
"

import sys
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
REPO = Path('.').resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO/'tenure'/'tenure_pipeline'))
from decision_year_cohort import build_decision_cohort_records
from decision_hero_prep import prepare_decision_hero_persons
panel = REPO/'tenure/tenure_pipeline/faculty_panel_with_pools.jsonl'
career = REPO/'tenure/tenure_pipeline/author_year_career_master.jsonl'
recs,_ = build_decision_cohort_records(panel, career)
df = pd.DataFrame(recs).dropna(subset=['pubs_per_career_year'])
persons,_ = prepare_decision_hero_persons(panel, career)
pdf = pd.DataFrame(persons)
merged = df.merge(pdf[['faculty_id','dept_loo_career_rate']], on='faculty_id')
n = len(merged)
for pct in [7,10,15,20,25]:
    k = max(1, int(round(pct/100*n)))
    print(f'top {pct}%: n={k}')
# within-year z bands
merged['z'] = merged.groupby('decision_year')['pubs_per_career_year'].transform(lambda s: (s-s.mean())/s.std() if s.std()>0 else 0)
for lo, hi in [(1,2),(1.5,2.5),(2,3),(1,3)]:
    sub = merged[(merged['z']>=lo)&(merged['z']<=hi)]
    print(f'z in [{lo},{hi}]: n={len(sub)}')
# top ventile on career rate (decile 10)
merged['decile'] = pd.qcut(merged['pubs_per_career_year'], 10, labels=False, duplicates='drop')
top_dec = merged[merged['decile']==merged['decile'].max()]
print('top decile career rate: n=', len(top_dec), 'tenure rate=', top_dec['tenure_event'].mean())
# Q8 bins within top 20%
top20 = merged.nlargest(max(1,int(round(0.20*n))), 'pubs_per_career_year')
print('top 20% tenure rate', top20['tenure_event'].mean(), 'n=', len(top20), '~', len(top20)//8, 'per bin if Q8 on LOO')
"

import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

datasets = {
    "football": "datasets/football/football_big_fish_player_season_panel/football_big_fish_player_season_panel.csv",
    "legends (league/LoL)": "datasets/legends/lol_big_fish_player_split_panel.csv",
    "nels88 (nlb88?)": "datasets/nels88/nels88_big_fish_panel.csv",
    "hsb80": "datasets/hsb80/hsb80_big_fish_panel.csv",
    "apache": "datasets/Apache/apache_big_fish_panel.csv",
}

for name, path in datasets.items():
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"\n=== {name}: MISSING {path} ===")
        continue
    df = pd.read_csv(p, low_memory=False, nrows=0)
    cols = list(df.columns)
    # full read for stats
    df = pd.read_csv(p, low_memory=False)
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"=== {name} ===")
    print(f"Rows: {len(df):,}  Cols: {len(cols)}")
    print(f"Size MB: {p.stat().st_size/1e6:.1f}")
    
    # key columns search
    key_patterns = ['performance', 'teammate', 'draft', 'tenure', 'promot', 'top_tier', 'eligible', 'own_', 'loo', 'pond', 'outcome', 'grade', 'gpa', 'college', 'career', 'wage', 'income', 'ability', 'peer', 'cohort', 'year', 'season', 'position', 'team']
    key_cols = [c for c in cols if any(k in c.lower() for k in key_patterns)]
    print(f"Key-ish columns ({len(key_cols)}):")
    for c in key_cols[:40]:
        fill = df[c].notna().mean()*100
        print(f"  {c}: {fill:.1f}%")
    if len(key_cols) > 40:
        print(f"  ... +{len(key_cols)-40} more")
    
    # sample unique counts for id cols
    for idc in ['player_period_id','player_id','playerid','student_id','id']:
        if idc in df.columns:
            print(f"  unique {idc}: {df[idc].nunique():,}")
    
    # outcome cols
    outcome_cols = [c for c in cols if any(x in c.lower() for x in ['draft', 'top_tier', 'tenure', 'promot', 'graduat', 'college', 'wage', 'income', 'outcome', 'y_'])]
    if outcome_cols:
        print("Outcome-like columns:")
        for c in outcome_cols[:15]:
            if df[c].dtype == 'bool' or df[c].nunique() <= 10:
                print(f"  {c}: {df[c].value_counts(dropna=False).head(5).to_dict()}")
            else:
                print(f"  {c}: fill={df[c].notna().mean()*100:.1f}%, nunique={df[c].nunique()}")

I am ready to assess the four new data directories.

The four directories map to college football, League of Legends, NELS:88, and High School & Beyond 1980. All follow the Big Fish panel schema with performance, peer context, outcomes, and pond definitions. Now comparing these against the dissertation requirements.

Football is the strongest candidate. It provides 168,000 player-season records across 65,000 athletes. The pond is the team roster, and the performance index is 42% overall with 100% coverage in the eligible cohort. The leave-one-out peer measure uses teammate mean performance excluding the focal player. This matches the HERO model structure well.

Football’s outcome is drafted status, but the eligible cohort contains only about 1,900 drafted athletes, making the outcome variable sparse. The dataset offers role-specific performance and recruiting ranks, yet snaps are missing for many positions, and public data limits opportunity and volume metrics. It spans just eleven seasons, so it is less clean than the basketball data.

Football is a strong second sports anchor for cross-domain replication. It can test whether the inverted-U and HERO effects hold in a different draft market, though position heterogeneity and sparse draft outcomes remain caveats.

The League of Legends dataset is the cleanest of the new batch. It tracks players through developmental leagues and captures top-tier promotion to professional play. Its performance index reaches 79.6 percent and leave-one-out peer coverage is 91.7 percent.

League of Legends offers explicit tiered promotion outcomes and roughly sixteen thousand eligible developmental records. Roster swapping creates an interesting congestion angle. Yet its advancement framing may be weaker for cross-domain validation than basketball or education. Same-role leave-one-out coverage is sparse at twenty-six point six percent. Outcome rates are modest and need censor filters.

League of Legends is the best structured alternative domain with a clear advancement gate. It is a strong fifth panel candidate.

The NELS:88 dataset tracks tenth-grade students. The pond is the high school. The performance index is a baseline test score. Leave-one-out peer coverage is ninety-six point six percent. The outcome is bachelor’s degree attainment by two thousand. About thirty-six percent of the minimum ten sample achieve this. It complements tenure data in the education domain. It is a national representative survey with weights.

The NELS:88 dataset contains roughly seven thousand observations with at least ten peers, which is adequate for the HERO model. The binary degree outcome is clean. However, the sample is limited to tenth-grade students rather than full school cohorts. Peer context is measured at a single point, and the outcome is observed over twelve years later. Attainment does not function as a competitive selection gate like drafting or tenure. The total sample is the smallest of the four datasets. It is medium-high for education cross-domain testing, though the selection mechanism is weaker than in sports or tenure.

HSB80 is the largest new dataset with roughly twenty-two thousand observations. It separates sophomore and senior cohorts, offering robustness checks. Peer leave-one-out coverage is ninety-nine point nine percent. The outcome is college attendance and bachelor’s degree completion by 1986. It includes rich covariates such as SES and GPA. The main downside is its dated 1980s institutional context.

I looked under `datasets/` — quick naming map first, since the folder names don’t exactly match what you typed:

| You said | Actual path | What it is |
|----------|-------------|------------|
| **football** | `datasets/football/` | FBS college football → NFL draft |
| **league** | `datasets/legends/` | League of Legends esports (dev → top-tier promotion) |
| **nlb88** | `datasets/nels88/` | NELS:88 (8th-grade cohort, 10th-grade school pond) |
| **hsb80** | `datasets/hsb80/` | HS&B:80 (sophomore + senior cohorts) |

All four are Alex’s **“Big Fish”** panels: own performance (Â analog), leave-one-out peer context, pond/unit ID, and a downstream advancement/outcome flag. That’s the same skeleton as MBB and tenure, which is why they’re worth taking seriously.

---

## Overall verdict

**Yes — all four could be useful**, but for different jobs in the dissertation:

| Dataset | Usefulness | Best role |
|---------|------------|-----------|
| **Legends (LoL)** | **High** | Fourth empirical domain with a real advancement gate |
| **Football** | **High** | Second *sports/draft* replication of MBB |
| **NELS88** | **Medium–high** | Education “small pond” complement to tenure |
| **HSB80** | **Medium** | Larger education robustness check; cohort-split work |

None replace MBB or tenure as anchors. They extend **cross-domain** coverage and give Alex’s Big Fish framework more places to land.

---

## 1. Football — strong MBB parallel, with role gaps

**~168K** player-season rows · **~70K** in `eligible_analysis_cohort` · **2014–2024**

| HERO slot | Column | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Unit | `player_period_id` (player × team × season) | Same grain as MBB season stints |
| Â | `own_performance_index` | 100% in eligible cohort; ~42% overall (many non-eligible rows) |
| Peer LOO | `teammate_mean_performance_excl_self` | 99.9% filled |
| Y | `drafted_next_draft` | ~**2.7%** in eligible cohort (~1,900 picks) |

**Why it’s useful:** Draft-as-advancement, team-as-pond, role-specific performance — structurally closest to MBB after LoL. Large eligible N supports HERO porch plots and maybe CCT-style band probes.

**Caveats:**
- Draft rate is thin (~1 in 37 eligible seasons) — tail bins will be sparse, like tenure Act II.
- **OL / low-volume roles** lack snaps; performance is missing or proxy-only for many rows.
- Only ~11 seasons; recruiting ranks help as priors but aren’t a full ability fix.

**COMPASS read:** Worth a **`football_sandbox/`** pass mirroring MBB basic plots + one HERO porch. Best headline: *“inverted-U / peer context replicates in a second draft market.”* Position heterogeneity is a feature (QB/WR vs OL), not a bug — but analyze by `position_group`.

---

## 2. League (`legends/`) — best-structured new domain

**~67K** split stints · **84 columns** · already mapped in `datasets/legends/README.md`

| HERO slot | Column | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Pond | team in a **developmental** league split | Explicit tier structure |
| Â | `own_performance_index` | 79.6% |
| Peer LOO | `teammate_mean_performance_excl_self` | 91.7% — primary LOO candidate |
| Y | `top_tier_debut_within_1y` / `_2y` | 3,052 / 4,456 positives; use `full_*_followup` for censoring |
| Filter | `eligible_developmental_cohort` | ~16K dev rows for HERO |

**Why it’s useful:** Alex built this specifically for you. Dev-league → top-tier promotion is a clean advancement gate (not just attainment). Tier labels (`developmental` / `top` / `other`) give a natural **environment vs advancement** story. N is healthy for porch + elite-pond probes.

**Caveats:** Higher roster churn than MBB; `same_role_mean_performance_excl_self` is sparse (27%). Esports may need one sentence of framing for non-gaming readers — but methodologically it’s a strong fourth panel.

**COMPASS read:** **Highest priority** of the four for a full sandbox (`legends_sandbox/` is already sketched in the README). Closest to “tenure/MBB but in a fresh domain.”

---

## 3. NELS88 (`nels88/`) — education small-pond, weaker selection story

**~10.5K** students · pond = **10th-grade high school** · outcome by **2000**

| HERO slot | Column | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Â | `own_performance_z` (baseline test) | 100% |
| Peer LOO | `peer_mean_loo`, `peer_mean_z_loo` | ~97% |
| Y | `bachelors_or_higher_by_2000` | ~**36%** in min-10 analytic sample (~7.2K rows) |
| Weights | `followup_weight_2000` | Survey weights available |

**Why it’s useful:** Education domain complements tenure without duplicating it. Pre-computed school LOO + degree outcome = fast HERO-style porch on “big fish in high school.” Connects to classic small-pond education literature.

**Caveats (Alex flagged these):**
- Sampled students **≠ full school cohort** — pond is noisy/incomplete.
- Outcome is **attainment**, not competitive top-K selection — score≠select is harder to motivate than draft/tenure/promotion.
- Single peer snapshot (10th grade) → long lag to Y (~12 years).

**COMPASS read:** Useful as **supporting cross-domain evidence** (“peer context predicts advancement-like outcomes in schools”), not as a headline domain unless you lean into attainment-as-advancement carefully.

---

## 4. HSB80 — bigger education N, more bookkeeping

**~23K** students · **Sophomore (12.6K) + Senior (10.3K)** — **analyze separately** (Alex)

| HERO slot | Column | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Â / LOO | Same Big Fish schema as NELS | LOO ~99% filled |
| Y | `bachelors_or_higher_by_1986`, `any_postsecondary_by_1986` | BA rate ~**11%** by 1986 in min-5 sample |
| Covariates | SES, GPA, school type/region | Richer than NELS for controls |

**Why it’s useful:** ~2× NELS N; good **robustness** if NELS porch shape holds. Sophomore vs senior gives two ponds at different ages.

**Caveats:** 1980s follow-up → low BA rate by 1986 (cohort still young). Same attainment-not-selection issue as NELS. Two cohorts = two separate pipelines, not one pooled panel.

**COMPASS read:** **Medium** — pair with NELS88 as a mini **education bundle** rather than standalone chapter material.

---

## How they fit the binding research frame

Your binding split — **environment (peer LOO) ≠ advancement (Y)** and **score ≠ select** — maps cleanly onto:

| Domain | Environment | Advancement Y | Selection clarity |
|--------|-------------|---------------|-------------------|
| MBB (anchor) | team LOO | draft | Strong |
| Tenure (anchor) | dept LOO | tenure | Strong |
| **Legends** | dev-team LOO | top-tier promotion | **Strong** |
| **Football** | team LOO | NFL draft | **Strong** |
| **NELS / HSB** | school LOO | degree attainment | **Weaker** |

So: **Legends + football** are the serious cross-domain extensions. **NELS + HSB** are valuable if the story is “peer context predicts downstream outcomes broadly,” with honest limits on the selection metaphor.

---

## Suggested priority (if you only have bandwidth for two)

1. **`legends/`** — full sandbox (BDP + HERO porch + dev-cohort filter); Alex already did the heavy lifting.
2. **`football/`** — eligible-cohort BDP deck; mirror MBB 3×3 where draft N allows.

Education panels can wait for a lighter pass: one porch each on `analytic_sample_min10` (NELS) and cohort-split HSB, mostly to see if the LOO–outcome curve **rhymes** with tenure/MBB.

---

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Here’s a LoL primer tuned for someone who knows Apex / War Thunder but not MOBAs — plus how it maps to Alex’s dataset.

---

## What League of Legends is (vs what you know)

**League of Legends (LoL)** is a **5v5 team MOBA** (multiplayer online battle arena), not a battle royale or vehicle sim.

| You know | LoL analogue |
|----------|----------------|
| Apex squad | Fixed **5-player team**, fixed **roles** for the whole match |
| Match → loot → circle | One **map**, one **objective** (destroy the enemy base) |
| War Thunder BR tiers | **Leagues/tiers** of pro competition (regional + “major” leagues) |
| Ranked ladder | **Pro circuit**: orgs, contracts, promotion between league levels |

Each match is roughly **25–45 minutes**. There is no respawn loop like Apex — deaths matter, but you come back after a timer. The win condition is destroying the enemy **Nexus** (home base) after pushing through lanes and towers.

---

## One match in plain English

1. **Two teams of five** spawn on opposite sides of **Summoner’s Rift** (the standard map).
2. Three **lanes** (top, mid, bot) plus **jungle** (between lanes). Minions spawn and push lanes; players **farm** gold/XP from minions and fights.
3. Each player picks a **champion** (character with unique abilities) and a **role**:
   - **Top** — usually bruisers/tanks  
   - **Jungle (jng)** — roams map, secures objectives  
   - **Mid** — mages/assassins, map center  
   - **Bot (adc)** — ranged damage + **Support (sup)** — peel/heal/engage  

4. Teams fight for **objectives** (towers, dragons, baron) to get stronger and open the map.
5. First team to destroy the enemy **Nexus** wins.

So compared to Apex: less about aim/movement in a shrinking zone, more about **macro** (when to fight, push, rotate), **team comp**, and **role discipline** over a long single round.

---

## Esports: how “pro LoL” is organized

Pro LoL is **league-based**, like soccer divisions in different countries — not one global queue.

### Regions and leagues

Major regions have their own leagues, e.g.:

- **LCK** — Korea (historically strongest)  
- **LPL** — China (huge, deep talent pool)  
- **LEC** — Europe  
- **LCS** — North America  

Each region runs **splits** (mini-seasons within a year, often Spring / Summer, sometimes others). Teams play a **regular season**, then **playoffs**, then sometimes **international** events (Worlds).

### Teams and rosters

- A **team** (e.g. T1, Cloud9) is an org with a **roster** of players — often **one starter per role**, sometimes substitutes.
- Players can **transfer** between teams/regions mid-career — Alex noted **more roster churn than college basketball**, which matters for your “pond” definition.

### Developmental (“academy”) leagues

This is the piece that matters most for your research.

Many top orgs run:

- **Main roster** in the **top-tier** league (LCK, LPL, etc.)  
- **Academy / challenger / “developmental”** roster in a **lower league** (e.g. **LCK Challengers**, **LDL** in China, **NACL** in NA)

Think: **G-League ↔ NBA**, or **minor league ↔ MLB** — same org brand, different competitive tier.

**Advancement Y in Alex’s panel:** a developmental player **debuts in a top-tier league** within 1–2 years (`top_tier_debut_within_1y` / `_2y`). That’s your draft/tenure analog: scarce “made it to the show” outcome.

---

## What Alex’s dataset is measuring

Each row is roughly: **one player stint** on a **team** in a **league split**, at a **position**.

| Research term | LoL reality |
|---------------|-------------|
| **Pond** | That team’s roster in that split (teammates you’re compared to) |
| **Â (own ability)** | `own_performance_index` — composite from match stats (damage, gold, KDA, vision, lane diffs, etc.) |
| **Peer LOO** | `teammate_mean_performance_excl_self` — how strong your teammates were, excluding you |
| **Environment** | Which **league tier** (`developmental` vs `top` vs `other`) |
| **Advancement** | Promoted to **top-tier** play within the follow-up window |

**Developmental cohort** (~16K rows): players in academy/second-tier leagues where “graduation” to LCK/LPL/etc. is still a live question.

---

## Stats people care about (why the columns look weird)

Oracle’s Elixir (Alex’s source) aggregates **per-game** stats into stint-level rates:

- **Damage / gold / CS per minute** — output and farming  
- **KDA, kill participation** — fight impact  
- **Vision score, wards** — map control (especially support/jungle)  
- **Gold/XP/CS diff @10/@15** — “did you win lane early?”  

Different **roles** have different jobs — a support with low damage can still be elite. That’s why there’s both team-wide LOO and (sparser) **same-role** LOO.

---

## Mental model for your dissertation story

- **MBB:** star on a loaded college roster → NBA draft  
- **Tenure:** productive assistant in a strong department → tenure  
- **LoL:** strong performer on a **developmental** roster → **top-tier league debut**

The **big fish / small pond** question: does being the standout on a weak academy team (low teammate LOO) vs a strong academy team (high LOO) predict who actually **gets promoted** — holding own skill roughly fixed?

Same binding split: **environment (pond quality) ≠ advancement (promotion)**; performance index **scores** talent, orgs **select** who moves up.

---

## Three jargon terms you’ll see in the CSV

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Split** | Sub-season within a year (e.g. Spring 2024) |
| **League tier** | `developmental` / `top` / `other` — Alex’s manual mapping |
| **Position** | top / jng / mid / bot / sup — fixed role for that stint |

---

If you want a follow-up, I can do a **one-page “LoL for the data story talk track”** (what to say on panel 1 of a future 3×3 deck) or walk through a **single example row** from the CSV as a narrative.
